Two formalin-fixed & paraffin-embedded (FFPE) breast cancer tissue blocks were obtained from Discovery Life Sciences. Sample #1 was annotated by a pathologist to be T2N1M0, Stage II-B, ER+/HER2+/PR−. Sample #2 was characterized as stage pT2 pN1a pMX, ER−/HER2+/PR−. Corresponding dissociated tumor cells for Sample #1, fresh frozen (FF) in liquid nitrogen, were also sampled from the same 2.5 cm biopsy. For the Chromium Flex workflow, two 25 μm curls were pooled as a single replicate. 5 μm sections from Sample #1 were taken from the FFPE tissue using a microtome. Two replicate 5 μm sections were taken each for Visium CytAssist and Xenium. A 5 μm section was also taken from Sample #2 for Xenium.

The clinical samples and related information obtained in this study were all approved by the Ethics Committee of Jiangsu University, and all patients gave written informed consent. They were diagnosed with diabetes according to the diagnostic criteria of China's Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes (2020), and CT of lower limbs showed significant calcification. In addition, patients who received diabetic foot surgery according to the Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Diabetic Foot in China (2019) were included in the study.The fresh tissues isolated from 4 patients were divided into calcified group (n=3) and noncalcified group (n=3) according to the relative position of CT images and vascular stiffness. After dead cells were removed, the samples were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 platform.

We obtained tissue blocks of postmortem human brain containing dACC from 10 neurotypical adult brain donors. We used the 10x Genomics Visium and 3’ Single Cell Gene Expression platforms to generate paired spatial transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA-seq data of the human dACC. Ten neurotypical control postmortem human brain donors were selected for the single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic study of the nucleus accumbens (NAc). We generated an integrated atlas with the two datasets of the human postmortem NAc to better understand the anatomical organization of heterogeneous medium spiny neuron (MSN) cell types. We identified multiple transcriptionally-distinct populations of MSNs that were organized in continuous gradients across the NAc.  *************************************************************** Raw files for human/patient samples are being made available in dbGaP (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gap/) for controlled access to the personally identifiable sequence data. ***************************************************************

records.title: The Developing Niche Regulates Engrafted Muscle Stem Cell Retention in Dystrophic and Regenerating Skeletal Muscle
records.summary: Cell therapies for skeletal muscle have limited ability to support long term engraftment and functional requirements of skeletal muscle including in diseased settings. Establishment of a myogenic niche is critical for PAX7+ muscle cell persistence including for cell therapies such those derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). However, the process for stem cell niche formation from engrafted muscle cells including in dystrophic environments, remains unclear. Using spatial RNA sequencing, we profiled the myogenic niche formation at seven early and late time points including in healthy and dystrophic muscle and after secondary injury. Surprisingly, we found a global decreases in genes involved with niche formation after 1 day in vivo paralleling a decrease in total engrafted cell number. We also found significant transcriptomic differences between engrafted PAX7 SMPCs in wild type compared to dystrophic muscle, and a reduction in niche maturity in response to injury in diseased mice. Among many candidates, we found MEGF10 is expressed during initial niche formation but lost overtime in wildtype and is persistent during the secondary injury process in mdx-D2-NSG mice. Due to MEGF10’s role in disease and niche establishment, we used CRISPR gene editing to generate a doxycyc
evidence: Using spatial RNA sequencing, we profiled the myogenic niche formation at seven early and late time points including in healthy and dystrophic muscle and after secondary injury.

We then performed spatial transcriptomics on engrafted MEGF10+ SMPCs and determined that enhanced cell-myofiber binding through NOTCH signaling and Tenascin-C was occurring while down regulating cell-matrix binding.

records.title: The Developing Niche Regulates Engrafted Muscle Stem Cell Retention in Dystrophic and Regenerating Skeletal Muscle [RNA-seq]
records.summary: Cell therapies for skeletal muscle have limited ability to support long term engraftment and functional requirements of skeletal muscle including in diseased settings. Establishment of a myogenic niche is critical for PAX7+ muscle cell persistence including for cell therapies such those derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). However, the process for stem cell niche formation from engrafted muscle cells including in dystrophic environments, remains unclear. Using spatial RNA sequencing, we profiled the myogenic niche formation at seven early and late time points including in healthy and dystrophic muscle and after secondary injury. Surprisingly, we found a global decreases in genes involved with niche formation after 1 day in vivo paralleling a decrease in total engrafted cell number. We also found significant transcriptomic differences between engrafted PAX7 SMPCs in wild type compared to dystrophic muscle, and a reduction in niche maturity in response to injury in diseased mice. Among many candidates, we found MEGF10 is expressed during initial niche formation but lost overtime in wildtype and is persistent during the secondary injury process in mdx-D2-NSG mice. records.title: TDP-43 toxic gain of function links ALS, FTD and Alzheimer’s Disease through splicing dysregulation
records.summary: Spatial transcriptomics of the human anterior hippocampus across LATE-NC (limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathological change) stages. Xenium In Situ was performed on anterior hippocampal sections from 24 post-mortem donors: 12 with LATE-NC stage 0 (no TDP-43 pathology) and 12 with LATE-NC stage 2 or 3 (extensive phosphorylated TDP-43 pathology). A 480-plex probe panel was used, including custom probes targeting cryptic exons (in 77 transcripts, including STMN2) and probes for specific APP mRNA isoforms (APP695 and APP751/770). The data were generated to relate TDP-43 pathology to STMN2 cryptic exon and APP isoform splicing within the hippocampal microenvironment. This series provides, per donor, the raw morphology image and decoded transcripts, the resegmented cell-by-feature matrix and cell and nucleus boundaries, and a per-cell table (quality-control flag, cell type and hippocampal subfield labels) for 626,260 segmented cells, of which 499,356 pass quality control (all 24 donors included).

records.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of primary lung adenocarcinomas and lymph node metastases
records.summary: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibits substantial intratumoral heterogeneity, and the spatial organization of malignant and stromal compartments associated with lymph node metastasis remains incompletely understood. We generated spatial transcriptomic profiles of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded primary LUAD specimens and lymph node metastasis tissue microarray slides using the 10x Genomics Visium platform. These data were used to compare spatial transcriptional features of primary malignant regions with lymph node malignant populations and to investigate tumor–stroma-associated transcriptional programs related to nodal metastasis. This GEO series contains processed spatial gene-expression data and associated spatial information corresponding to the sequencing data deposited under BioProject PRJNA1427751.

records.title: Transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling uncovers shared muscle-intrinsic pathways in spinal muscle atrophy and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
records.summary: single nucleus RNA sequencing Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) are motor neuron diseases characterized by progressive muscle wasting, yet the contribution of intrinsic muscle pathology remains unclear. We applied single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing to skeletal muscle biopsies from SMA patients, ALS patients, and healthy controls. Nuclei were isolated and processed using the 10x Genomics Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiomic ATAC + Gene Expression platform to generate paired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq libraries for each sample. Sequencing was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 instrument.

records.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals HER2/AR-associated heterogeneity and alternative surface targets in salivary duct carcinoma
records.summary: Salivary duct carcinoma (SDC) is an aggressive malignancy in which HER2- and androgen receptor (AR)-directed therapies are used for recurrent or metastatic disease, although therapeutic responses remain heterogeneous. We performed spatial transcriptomic profiling of four SDC specimens to characterize intratumoral heterogeneity of HER2- and AR-associated transcriptional states and to identify alternative cell-surface therapeutic targets. Spatial mapping revealed heterogeneous distributions of HER2-associated, AR-associated, dual-associated, and HER2/AR-non-associated regions within individual tumors. Surfaceome-based screening identified several candidate targets with low expression in matched normal salivary gland tissue and broad tumor coverage.

records.title: Placental NOD1-NOD2-RIPK2 Expression and Innate Immune Activation in Congenital CMV Infection
records.summary: The role of the pattern recognition receptors nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain 1 and 2 (NOD1 and NOD2) and their downstream receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (RIPK2) in congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection and transplacental transmission has not been previously characterized. We hypothesized that CMV infection during pregnancy would alter placental expression of NOD1, NOD2, and downstream signaling through RIPK2. We examined differences in the timing, localization, and expression of NOD1, NOD2, and RIPK2 in CMV-infected and uninfected placentas. Seven CMV-infected placentas (one from early gestation, six from late gestation) and 36 uninfected placentas (23 from early and 13 from late gestation) were collected for immunohistochemical staining. NOD1 and NOD2 were detected in syncytiotrophoblast cells (STB), and RIPK2 was detected in villous macrophages (Hofbauer cells). NOD1 exhibited crisp staining of the STB layer in placentas from early and late gestation, regardless of CMV infection. STB cells also stained positively for NOD2 during both early and late gestation in infected and uninfected placentas. records.title: Polyamines and Epithelial barrier loss during HIV infection
records.summary: Despite effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), people with HIV (PWH) continue to experience chronic oral mucosal disease characterized by persistent T-cell inflammation, regulatory T cell (Treg) dysfunction, impaired CD8+ tissue resident cell (TRM) immunity and microbial dysbiosis. Emerging evidence identifies dysregulated polyamine me-tabolism and mucosal T cell dysregulation as key mediators of these pathological processes. The paradoxical dose-dependent effects of polyamines on epithelial barrier integrity are critically discussed, and a unified mechanistic model is proposed. It also highlights single-cell transcriptomic data from our laboratory that implicates epithelial cell barrier dysfunction in PWH and offers a perspective of how it may worsen persistent inflammation even after combined anti-retroviral treatment. records.title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct pineal neoplasm with neuroendocrine and epithelial differentiation (PINNED)
records.summary: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and that is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range: 7–75 years). Histopathological analyses demonstrated a cell-dense malignancy showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring-like cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to Papillary Tumors of the Pineal Region (PTPR). records.title: Intrapatient heterogeneity and targeting microenvironment resistance mechanisms in melanoma metastasis
records.summary: Intrapatient tumor heterogeneity contributes to immunotherapy and targeted therapy resistance in metastatic cutaneous melanoma. Over 50% of melanoma patients develop brain metastases (MBM) during disease progression and these patients have a very poor prognosis. To assess how tumors persist through treatments and adapt to and rely on organ-specific microenvironments, we utilized samples from a patient LOGIC2 clinical trial who received anti-CTLA4, BRAFi/MEKi, and BRAFi/MEKi+CDK4/6i treatments. Seven short-term melanoma cultures (STMCs) were established from different metastatic site biopsies at chronological time points throughout the patient’s treatment and post-mortem. While an initial treatment naïve metastatic tumor in the breast was BRAFV600E mutant, NRASQ61 mutations were detected after treatment with CDK4/6i in the bone and ovary metastases. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing and identified that STMC consisted of 2-10 different subpopulations. In vitro, all STMCs were resistant to CDK4/6i, but exhibited varying degrees of response to BRAFi/MEKi. The growth factor receptor, HER3, was upregulated in the MBM STMC and detected in other MBM patient datasets. records.title: Ruxolitinib acts as a senomorphic therapy to alleviate choroidal neovascularization progression via inhibition of the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway
records.summary: Background: Cellular senescence plays a key role in the pathogenesis of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). Senomorphic therapy, which targets the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), holds promise for treating age-related diseases; however, effective senomorphic treatments for nAMD remain lacking. Methods: We screened a panel of senomorphic agents in bleomycin- and ionizing radiation (IR)-induced senescent ARPE-19 cells to identify a lead compound for nAMD. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to explore JAK-STAT signaling activation. Ruxolitinib and siRNA were used to validate the role of the JAK1/2-STAT3 pathway in senescent retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). A laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV) model was established in Brown-Norway rats for in vivo studies. Results: Ruxolitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, most effectively suppressed SASP factors and complement C3 expression while restoring pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) levels in senescent ARPE-19 cells. Knockdown of JAK1 or JAK2 significantly reversed the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), C3, and PEDF. records.summary: Human malformations of cortical development (MCDs) are rare disorders, which have been associated with conserved brain architecture with fewer neurons (microcephaly) or associated with absent or abnormal gyri (lissencephaly). A more severe disorder is microlissencephaly, in which both the size and the folding pattern of the brain are affected, and results from a loss of function of the NDE1 gene. In this study, the role of NDE1 in the developing brain is investigated with different human brain organoids systems. Organoids which arise from NDE1 KO embryonic stem cells line are considerably smaller and grow slower than control organoids and exhibit mitosis defects. records.title: Ecotypes of triple-negative breast cancer in response to chemotherapy [Visium]
records.summary: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype that is frequently treated with chemotherapy, but only half of the patients respond well and have good clinical outcome1,2. Here we leveraged pretreatment tissue samples from treatment-naive patients with TNBC who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and performed single-cell transcriptomic analysis of 427,857 cells from 101 patients and spatial transcriptomic analysis of 44 patients. We classified TNBC tumours into 4 patient-level subtypes (archetypes) using the cancer-cell gene expression and identified 13 metaprograms that reflect intra-tumoural heterogeneity at the single-cell level. The TNBC tumour microenvironment consisted of 49 immune and stromal cell states, many of which were reprogrammed relative to normal breast tissues. Furthermore, we identified eight distinct cellular communities (ecotypes) on the basis of the co-occurrences of cancer cells and tumour microenvironment cell types, and their spatial organization in tissues. In contrast to previous studies on T cells, our data show the importance of macrophage subtypes and cancer-cell metaprograms for interferon signalling, human leukocyte antigen expression and cell cycle activity that are associated with a good response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. records.title: A cellular and vascular atlas of the breast tumor microenvironment with multi-resolution spatial transcriptomics [10x Visium HD]
records.summary: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of human breast tumors to define high endothelial venule (HEV) states associated with tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs). Includes 10x Genomics Visium data from 40 sections (33 tumor sections from 32 tumors, one profiled in duplicate, plus 7 matched uninvolved lymph nodes), Visium HD data from 4 tumors and Xenium data from 6 tumors. We identify a stromal "primed" HEV state carrying STING-associated and adhesive programs, and a mature TLS-associated state additionally marked by lymphotoxin-β receptor signaling, perivascular CCL19/CCL21 expression, and SPP1. Together these define a candidate endothelial maturation axis linked to TLS organization.

records.title: Single-nucleus multiome (snRNA-seq + snATAC-seq) of MCF7 breast cancer cells under acute acidosis, chronic acid adaptation, and return to physiological pH
records.summary: Extracellular acidosis is a persistent feature of solid tumors. Our study shows that adaptation of breast cancer cells to acidosis is accompanied by plastic rewiring of sphingolipid metabolism centered on ceramide turnover. To ask whether these metabolic changes are associated with transcriptional and chromatin reprogramming, and whether such reprogramming is transient or stable, we performed single-nucleus multiome profiling (joint snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq, 10x Genomics) of MCF7 cells under four conditions: control (pH 7.4), acute acidosis (pH 6.5 for 3 days), chronic acid adaptation (pH 6.5 for more than 3 months), and return of acid-adapted cells to pH 7.4 for 3 days. Transcriptionally similar nuclei were aggregated into metacells, a transcription factor regulatory network was inferred with ARACNe3, and transcription factor activity was estimated with VIPER to score the regulatory drive toward four ceramide clearance pathways (S1P, C1P, SM and GSL) and to identify candidate regulators of each pathway.

records.title: EHF/ESE3 loss causes prostate epithelial cell plasticity and cancer (RWPE - RNA-seq data)
records.summary: RNA-seq of coding RNA Phenotypic plasticity associated with epithelial to mesenchymal transition occurs in the late stage of several types of cancers and results in metastatic spread and enhanced resistance to therapy. Understanding these events is important to prevent and cure this aberrant conversion. Intriguingly, primary prostate tumors are androgen-sensitive and display a strong luminal identity. In contrast, aggressive prostate tumors are characterized by change of identity, insensitivity to androgen ablation therapy. Thus, an active mechanism maintains the normal physiologic androgen responsive status preventing plasticity. In this study, we show for the first time that conditional knockout of the epithelial specific ETS factor EHF/ESE3, which is a top ranking expressed TF in the normal prostate, is sufficient to determine a dramatic loss of cell identity and transformation. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that loss of EHF/ESE3 reactivates an aberrant ambiguous cell program with acquisition of endothelial and stromal features. Astonishingly, crossing the cEHF-KO mice with TMPRSS2-ERG mice resulted in complete conversion of the epithelial component to a stromal like status supported by tracing the epithelial cells TMPRSS2ERG/eGFP positive. records.summary: RNA-seq of coding RNA from single cells Allogeneic stem cell transplantation remains a cornerstone of the treatment of some hematological malignancies, although it is still associated with a significant morbidity and mortality which are mainly related to graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). NF-kB signaling pathways play a determining role in the pathogenesis of the disease in part through OX40 receptor signaling in donor T cells. In order to determine whether NIK inhibition could become a therapeutic strategy against GVHD in humans, we assessed the ability of the NIK inhibitor SMI1 at preventing GVHD in a humanized mouse model combining xenogeneic and allogeneic GVHD. NSG-HLA-A2-HHD mice were transplanted with human HLA-A2 negative peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) on day 0 and treated twice daily with SMI1 from day 1 to day 20. Single cell RNA sequencing and TCR repertoire analyses were performed on human CD3+ T cells isolated from day 20 blood samples. records.title: Modelling KRAS Mutations in KMT2A-MLLT3 AML Promotes Leukemic Progression and Transcriptomic Remodeling
records.summary: KRAS mutations are frequently detected in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with KMT2A-MLLT3 (KM3) rearrangements, yet their biological impact remains poorly understood. Using a humanized in vivo KM3 AML model, we introduced KRAS G13D or G12C point mutations via CRISPR-Cas9 in CD34⁺ cord blood cells to mimic subclonal events observed in patients. We found that KRAS mutations significantly accelerated leukemia onset and increased leukemic stem cell (LSC) frequency by over 20-fold, without altering the surface phenotype. Transcriptomic profiling revealed extensive gene expression reprogramming, including upregulation of stemness- and quiescence-associated genes such as IKZF2 and ALOX15, and activation of inflammatory and NF-κB signaling pathways. Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovered a distinct population with a conventional type 1 dendritic cell (cDC1)-like transcriptional profile, emerging exclusively in KRAS-mutated leukemias and expressing key LSC regulators. This suggests that KRAS mutations not only enhance aggressiveness but also drive cellular heterogeneity within the leukemic clone. records.title: In situ targeted gene expression analysis of primary and metastatic prostate biopsies
records.summary: Prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance are associated with substantial tumor cell plasticity and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. In this study, we performed in situ targeted gene expression profiling of primary and metastatic prostate cancer biopsies using the 10x Genomics Xenium platform to characterize tumor cell states and their interactions with stromal and immune cell populations while preserving tissue architecture. Comparative analyses were performed to identify differences between primary and metastatic disease and to evaluate changes in tumor cellular composition and transcriptional states. This dataset provides a spatially resolved resource for investigating tumor heterogeneity, lineage plasticity, metastatic progression, and therapy-associated cellular changes in advanced prostate cancer.
evidence: In this study, we performed in situ targeted gene expression profiling of primary and metastatic prostate cancer biopsies using the 10x Genomics Xenium platform to characterize tumor cell states and their interactions with stromal and immune cell populations while preserving tissue architecture.

records.title: Coupled MAPK output and lineage identity define modes of osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma
records.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma comprises ~20% of non-small cell lung cancers; nearly all patients relapse on EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitors. To study how tumor evolution and cell state plasticity shape therapeutic resistance, we mapped transcriptional state differentiation from single nucleus RNA sequencing alongside secondary mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) alterations from clinical genomic sequencing across 83 patient samples. Contrasting treatment-naïve, minimal residual disease and progressive disease reveals a coupling of MAPK signaling and lineage identity, leading to archetypal modes of resistance: MAPK reactivation with retained adenocarcinoma identity, and lineage plasticity coincident with MAPK-low transcriptional states. Poorly differentiated states are rare but detectable pre-treatment and enriched at progression with or without overt histologic transformation, and confirmed in matched longitudinal samples. Lastly, we report a convergent phenotypic bottleneck at minimal residual disease, motivating a proactive therapeutic strategy guided by signaling output, lineage identity and genomic context.
evidence: To study how tumor evolution and cell state plasticity shape therapeutic resistance, we mapped transcriptional state differentiation from single nucleus RNA sequencing alongside secondary mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) alterations from clinical genomic sequencing across 83 patient samples.
records.overall_design: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 73 EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma specimens spanning treatment-naive, minimal residual disease and progressive disease states (GSE292469), integrated with Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics of matched treatment-naive and progressive disease sections from five patients (GSE342824).

records.title: Coupled MAPK output and lineage identity define modes of osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma [Xenium in situ]
records.summary: Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics of matched treatment-naive (TN) and progressive disease (PD) FFPE tumor sections from five patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma, resolving the spatial organisation of the tumor lineage states that accompany EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance. Ten sections (five TN/PD pairs) were assayed with a 389-plex panel: the Xenium Human Lung panel v1.1 (289 predesigned targets) plus a 100-gene custom add-on selected to resolve alveolar, basal and neuroendocrine lineage states together with EGFR mutant and wild-type alleles. This Series contains 1,516,917 segmented cells. Per-section raw and processed outputs from Xenium Onboard Analysis 4.0.1.0 are provided, together with a Series-level annotation table covering the 1,400,257 cells that passed the >10-transcript threshold used for cell-type calling. The matched single-nucleus RNA sequencing cohort is deposited separately as GSE292469.

records.title: Single-cell Multiome Analysis of Chromatin State and Transcriptome in the Human Basal Ganglia
records.summary: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generate a single-cell multiome atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical adult human donors. This atlas resolves cell-type- and regional-specific landscape of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements, and delineates gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We find that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors provides distinctive molecular descriptors of neuronal cell identity in basal ganglia. Integration with matched MERFISH spatial transcriptomics further uncovers regional heterogeneity in epigenomic and transcriptional programs. Finally, we use this atlas to interpret non-coding risk variants associated with neuropsychiatric disorders and to construct a deep learning model that predicts gene regulatory activities and variant effects. Together, this work provides a multimodal regulatory framework for understanding human basal ganglia organization, evolution, and disease genetics.
evidence: Integration with matched MERFISH spatial transcriptomics further uncovers regional heterogeneity in epigenomic and transcriptional programs.

records.summary: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 73 EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma specimens sampled across three treatment states: treatment-naive (TN), minimal residual disease (MRD) on EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy, and progressive disease (PD). The cohort is unmatched across states; clinical annotation is available for all samples and MSK-IMPACT genomic profiling for 68 of 73. One specimen (MRD2) was sampled as two cores of the same resection and sequenced as two libraries, so the 73 specimens are represented by 74 Samples. This Series contains 457,724 nuclei passing quality control across the 74 libraries. Sixty-two libraries were prepared with the 10x Genomics Chromium 3' v3.1 kit; the twelve libraries with LX identifiers were prepared with the Chromium 3' v4 kit. All were aligned with Cell Ranger 7.1.0 against GRCh38. Two Series-level processed files are provided: a raw UMI count matrix spanning all samples (counts.h5), and a cell metadata table (cell_metadata.tsv.gz) giving each nucleus its sample of origin, core of origin, treatment state, QC statistics, doublet scores, a tumor-cell flag, and one of nine cell-type annotations (tumor cell, epithelial, T-cell, B-cell, plasma cell, myeloid, mast cell, fibroblast, endothelial). records.overall_design: Tumor specimens were obtained from 73 patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (73 specimens across 74 libraries; one specimen was sampled as two cores of the same resection and sequenced twice). Each specimen represents a single treatment state: treatment-naive (TN, n=28; prior to any osimertinib exposure), minimal residual disease (MRD, n=14; on osimertinib after maximal tumor shrinkage and before progression), or progressive disease (PD, n=31; at radiographic progression on osimertinib). The cohort comprised 42 female and 31 male patients, median age 63 years (range 34-78) at first sampling. Specimens were collected at biopsy or surgical resection between 2017 and 2024 and flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen (median ischemic time 92 minutes); resections were macrodissected to enrich for tumor-rich regions before freezing. Most specimens were primary lung (n=49), the remainder bone and soft tissue (n=7), liver (n=6), lymph node (n=4), brain (n=3), locoregional metastases (n=2) and pleura (n=2). Nuclei were isolated on a Singulator 200, FACS-sorted on 7-AAD, and libraries prepared with the 10x Genomics Chromium 3' v3.1 kit (62 libraries) or Chromium 3' v4 kit (12 libraries), ~10,000 nuclei per sample. All specimens were collected under MSKCC IRB protocols #12-245 and #06-107.

records.title: Single-cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients With Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-β Signaling
records.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. records.title: Single-Nuclei Mapping of Immune and Glial Diversity in Pediatric Neuroinflammatory Diseases: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis and Rasmussen Encephalitis
records.summary: Background: Rasmussen encephalitis (RE) and primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS) are rare pediatric neuroinflammatory diseases characterized by intractable epilepsy and vascular inflammation, respectively. Their immunopathological mechanisms remain poorly defined, and, to our knowledge, single-cell transcriptomic data from pediatric PACNS brain tissue have not been reported. Methods: We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of cortical tissue from one 12-year-old girl with biopsy-confirmed PACNS, two children with RE undergoing hemispherectomy, and two non-neurological pediatric postmortem controls. After CellBender ambient-RNA correction, doublet removal and reference-based annotation (Allen Human brain reference), 18,401 nuclei were integrated with Harmony. Microglia and oligodendrocytes were sub-clustered and compared between groups with cell-level differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis of the full ranked gene list, with sensitivity analyses excluding HLA, immediate-early and ribosomal/mitochondrial genes. Because only one PACNS donor was available, all comparisons are exploratory. records.title: Macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition as a potential driver of early renal fibrosis in IgA nephropathy: insights from single-cell RNA sequencing analysis
records.summary: Background: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and renal failure. Renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis is a predictor of a poor kidney outcome, and macrophages are involved into this process. However, the precise phenotyping mechanisms of macrophages at the early stage of IgAN, particularly how they initiate fibrogenesis, remain largely unknown. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis was conduct on renal biopsy specimens from IgAN patients, as well as membranous nephropathy (MN) control samples and adjacent healthy kidney control samples from the public GEO database. After quality control and batch correction, unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis and pathway enrichment analysis were carried out. Subsequently, an IgAN mouse model was established to investigate the fibrosis severity and potential mechanism. Results: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in the renal immune microenvironment in IgAN, characterized by an increase in macrophages and fibroblasts and a decrease in proximal tubular cells. Macrophages in IgAN exhibit M2 phenotyping, with high expression of CD163 and low expression of Fc gamma receptor IIIa (FCGR3A). records.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumor-infiltrating NY-ESO-1 TCR-T cells with WT or ITAM M3 CD3ζ
records.summary: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize the transcriptional states of tumor-infiltrating NY-ESO-1-specific TCR-T cells expressing wild-type (WT) CD3ζ or the ITAM M3 CD3ζ variant. Human primary T cells were engineered to express the NY-ESO-1 TCR together with WT or ITAM M3 CD3ζ and adoptively transferred into NSG mice bearing A375 human melanoma xenografts. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) were isolated 10 days after TCR-T cell infusion. For each condition, TILs from three mice were pooled before single-cell RNA sequencing using the BD Rhapsody platform. The dataset was generated to investigate how ITAM M3-mediated recalibration of TCR signaling affects TCR-T cell functional state, including activation, cytotoxicity, exhaustion, proliferation, and stemness within the tumor microenvironment.

records.title: H3K18la in endothelial cells promotes tumor immunosuppression
records.summary: Tumor endothelial cells (TECs) play vital roles in tumor development. Herein, we found that TECs contribute to tumor immunosuppression by inducing Treg infiltration. The highly glycolytic tumor microenvironment elevated histone lactylation levels in TECs. After screening, we found that H3K18la was significantly upregulated in TECs as compared with normal endothelial cells. Combinational analysis of CUT& Tag and scRNA-seq demonstrated that hyperlactylation of H3K18 directly promoted CCL5 expression, which induced Treg infiltration and promoted tuomor immunosuppression.
evidence: Combinational analysis of CUT& Tag and scRNA-seq demonstrated that hyperlactylation of H3K18 directly promoted CCL5 expression, which induced Treg infiltration and promoted tuomor immunosuppression.

records.title: Longitudinal spatial mapping of tumor–immune microenvironment following electrochemotherapy of cutaneous melanoma metastases
records.summary: Background: Electrochemotherapy (ECT) utilizes reversible electroporation for localized chemotherapeutic delivery, where beyond local cytotoxicity, ECT acts as an in situ immunomodulator. However, the dynamic spatial orchestration of the TME that translates this localized therapy into potential abscopal-like responses in untreated lesions remains poorly understood. Methods: To uncover the mechanisms of evolving tumor microenvironment (TME) that dictate this immune activation, we applied Xenium spatial transcriptomics to longitudinally sampled in-transit cutaneous melanoma metastases from three patients, capturing baseline immune states and two distinct post-ECT intervals (two-to-three and nine-to-ten days). Furthermore, to explicitly characterize potential abscopal-like effects, biopsies were collected also from non-treated lesions. Following sample integration, we annotated cell types and identified functional subpopulations of key compartments, which we compared across treatment timepoints and patients. Further, we resolved functional spatial niches and identified spatially localized immune front, which we characterized and linked to patients' clinical responses. records.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of appendiceal adenocarcinoma reveals a low proportion of epithelial cells and a fibroblast enriched tumor microenvironment
records.summary: Appendiceal adenocarcinoma (AA) is an understudied gastrointestinal malignancy. Treatment is guided by its proximal counterpart, colorectal cancer (CRC), despite recent studies demonstrating AA’s unique mutational landscape and poor response to CRC chemotherapy. As the first application of single-cell technology to AA these data provide insight into the intratumor heterogeneity of AA and highlight the important contribution of the tumor microenvironment in this orphan disease. These results also reinforce multiple observations that AA is a unique disease entity from CRC and targeting the tumor microenvironment should be considered as a therapeutic strategy.

records.title: Local and circulating cytotoxic CD4 T cells are early markers of disease activity in pediatric Crohn’s disease
records.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) requires improved molecular and cellular stratification to guide therapy. In the PREDICT study, we profiled intestinal and blood T cells from treatment-naïve pediatric patients with IBD, disorders of gut–brain interaction controls, and healthy donors using single-cell RNA sequencing. Across 107 participants, we identify a population of clonally expanded cytotoxic CD4 T cells (CD4 CTL) enriched in the inflamed gut of patients with Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis. Cell–cell interaction analyses and validation in a mouse model implicate IL-27 in CD4 CTL differentiation. Elevated CD4 CTL frequencies in gut and peripheral blood at diagnosis are associated with subsequent poor outcome of anti-TNF therapy in pediatric CD. Findings in our identification cohort are validated in an independent cohort and through reanalysis of published datasets. Blood CD4⁺CXCR6⁺CD27⁻ T cells displayed a CD4 CTL transcriptional phenotype, supporting CD4 CTLs as a candidate blood-accessible biomarker for treatment stratification.
evidence: In the PREDICT study, we profiled intestinal and blood T cells from treatment-naïve pediatric patients with IBD, disorders of gut–brain interaction controls, and healthy donors using single-cell RNA sequencing.

records.title: Integrated transcriptomic and tissue profiling reveals imprinted-gene dysregulation and PEG10 upregulation in liposarcoma
records.summary: Liposarcoma is a rare cancer, comprising four major histological subtypes with distinct molecular features and limited therapeutic options in advanced disease. We investigated subtype-associated transcriptional programmes, imprinted-gene dysregulation and the expression context of PEG10 in liposarcoma. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on 16 independent liposarcoma tumours and five adjacent non-tumour tissues. PEG10 was further examined by RT-qPCR, RNA fluorescence in situ hybridisation (RNA-FISH), exploratory TCGA-SARC survival analysis and an external single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset of dedifferentiated liposarcoma. Transcriptomic profiling identified subtype-associated programmes and significant enrichment of imprinted genes in liposarcoma. PEG10 showed tumour-associated upregulation supported by RT-qPCR and RNA-FISH. PEG10 was detectable across all major subtypes, with the highest bulk transcript levels in myxoid liposarcoma, while RNA-FISH signal was higher in G3 than G2 tumours. In TCGA-SARC, higher PEG10 expression was associated with shorter overall survival, whereas DDLPS-specific analyses were not significant. External single-cell data localised PEG10 predominantly to tumour and cycling-cell populations and to angiogenesis- and invasion-associated tumour-cell states.
evidence: PEG10 was further examined by RT-qPCR, RNA fluorescence in situ hybridisation (RNA-FISH), exploratory TCGA-SARC survival analysis and an external single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset of dedifferentiated liposarcoma.

records.title: Single-cell regulatory genomics reveals coordinated myeloid and T-cell reprogramming in liver cirrhosis
records.summary: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on liver tissues from 3 cirrhotic patients and 3 non-cirrhotic controls, analyzing 43,745 high-quality cells. We investigated cellular composition, SCENIC regulon activity, pseudotime trajectories, and CellChat communication. Cirrhosis was associated with Mono1 depletion, expansion of inflammatory macrophages and regulatory T cells, dysregulated YY1/ETV6 regulons in myeloid cells, altered EOMES/KLF6 programs in cytotoxic T cells, and increased EP300/SP3 in Tregs, along with fibrosis-biased ligand-receptor signaling. Note: Raw sequencing data are not available because the sequencing company routinely clears data after two years; only processed expression matrices are provided.

records.title: A Viral Replication Level-Dependent Continuum of Transcriptional and MicroRNA Reprogramming in HIV-1-Infected Microglia Links Productive Infection to Neurocognitive-Associated Gene Networks [RNA-seq]
records.summary: Microglia are major targets of HIV-1 in the brain. Despite the effectiveness of antiviral therapy, infected microglia, including those containing a replication-defective provirus, can express viral RNA and proteins that contribute to neuroinflammation. However, the degree to which productive infection shapes the host response in microglia remains poorly defined. Using single cell RNA-seq of HIV-1-infected C20 microglia, we stratified cells by counts of HIV-1 reads with splice junctions into low- and high-infection groups, enabling us to resolve a graded rather than binary host transcriptional response. A core set of immune and cell-cycle pathways was induced regardless of infection level, but several programs reversed direction with increasing viral burden: interferon-α/γ and EMT/hypoxia signatures peaked at low infection, while high infection was marked by suppression of these signatures alongside induction of mTORC1/MYC signaling, ribosome biogenesis, RNA processing, and mitotic activity, accompanied by progressive loss of cytoskeletal, motility, and developmental gene programs. This pattern was reproduced in iPSC-derived microglia, supporting its generalizability beyond an immortalized line. records.title: Single-cell analysis reveals transcriptomic patterns in active macrophage activation syndrome and therapeutic potential of albumin-fused interleukin-10 in a mouse model
records.summary: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) and macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) are life-threatening hyperinflammatory conditions characterized by excessive immune activation and cytokine production. To clarify immune cell characteristics and identify potential therapeutic targets in MAS, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on bone marrow and peripheral blood samples from patients with newly developed MAS caused by diverse etiologies. To broaden the current knowledge of the immune landscape in the bone marrow, we performed scRNA-Seq of bone marrow cells and isolated blood leukocytes obtained from MAS patients using the Seq-Well.

records.title: Single-cell atlas reveals shared early microenvironmental remodeling in colorectal polypogenesis
records.summary: Colorectal polyps are the earliest precancerous lesions in colorectal carcinogenesis, but their common microenvironmental drivers remain incompletely defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on paired normal mucosal and colorectal polyp tissues from 3 patients with unselected lesions, including hyperplastic polyps and tubular adenomas. After quality control, 31,147 high-quality cells were obtained. Comparative analysis revealed four conserved hallmarks of colorectal polyps relative to normal mucosa: disrupted epithelial homeostasis characterized by stem cell expansion, Paneth cell reduction, and Wnt pathway activation; pro-inflammatory polarization of CD4+ T cells with increased Th17 cells and activation of NF-kB/IL-17-related pathways; functional reprogramming of CD8+ T cell subsets, especially decreased IELs with specialized immune functions; and extensive remodeling of immune-epithelial intercellular communication, including CD55-ADGRE5, MIF-CD74, and GZMA-PARD3 signaling axes. These data provide a single-cell atlas of shared microenvironmental changes in early colorectal polypogenesis.
evidence: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on paired normal mucosal and colorectal polyp tissues from 3 patients with unselected lesions, including hyperplastic polyps and tubular adenomas.

records.title: scRNA-seq of skin and PBMC samples of systemic sclerosis patients and healthy controls
records.summary: Skin and blood samples from systemic sclerosis (SSc) patients and healthy donors were analyzed using single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq). CCL19+ fibroblast was upregulated in the dermis of patients with SSc, and exhibited high expression of immuno-regulatory genes, including CCL19. CCL19 expression correlated with the severity of dermal fibrosis in SSc. The most significant ligand-receptor interaction from CCL19+ fibroblast to T cells in SSc skin was CCL19-CCR7. Furthermore, CCR7+ T cells in the fibrotic skin, particularly CCR7+CD8+ T cells, displayed enhanced stemness and cytotoxicity, actively interacting with extracellular matrix (ECM)-producing fibroblasts in SSc.

records.title: Type I regulatory T cells have overlapping phenotypes with circulating Tfh and Th1 in P. falciparum
records.summary: Immunity to P. falciparum malaria develops slowly, requiring repeated infection in areas of high transmission, and wanes rapidly in the absence of parasite exposure. Key to this immunity, is the development of antibodies which is supported by CD4⁺ T follicular helper (Tfh) cells that drive robust germinal centre responses. However, in malaria, the malaria-specific CD4⁺ T cell compartment in peripheral blood is dominated by Type 1 regulatory T cells (Tr1), which produce high levels of IL-10 in response to parasites. Tr1-like Tfh cells (Tfh10) have been reported in several settings of repeated antigen stimulation but have not been investigated in malaria. Here we used single-cell RNA sequencing and multiparameter flow cytometry to characterise malaria-specific Tfh and Tr1 cells in a longitudinal cohort of highly exposed individuals and assessed their persistence after transmission interruption. Malaria-specific Tfh and Tr1 cells shared overlapping profiles, and Tr1 cell-like transcriptional signatures and phenotypes were detectable within the Tfh cell compartment. Tfh10 cell subsets were the dominant phenotype of malaria-specific Tfh cells. Following disruption of malaria transmission, the frequencies of malaria-specific Tr1 and Tfh10 cells declined. records.title: Multi-lineage evolution of drug resistance via a keratin 17+ aberrant basaloid drug tolerant persister population in EGFR-mutant NSCLC
records.summary: We have an incomplete understanding of how EGFR-mutant drug tolerant persister cells (DTPCs) adapt to tolerate EGFR signaling blockade and whether these different mechanisms of resistance are present at baseline or emerge from a common DTPC population. In this study, we leveraged single cell RNA sequencing to comprehensively characterize phenotypes potentiating EGFR-mutant DTPCs and minimal residual disease states in part by sampling in vitro model systems. Using this and other single cell RNA sequencing data, we uncovered that a recurrent, novel KRT17+/KRT5- DTPC population harboring basaloid features and decreased alveolar lineage fidelity could give rise to diverse, multilineage mechanisms of targeted therapy resistance.

records.title: Tau A152T risk variant drives distinct cell type transcriptional signatures in AD and PSP
records.summary: The A152T point mutation is a rare genetic variant in the tau gene (MAPT) that is linked to risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia spectrum disorders, including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD). These efforts revealed that despite similar cell type composition across groups, A152T carriers exhibited distinct cell type-specific transcriptional changes in both AD and PSP. Differential expression analysis identified excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes and astrocytes as the most affected cell populations in AD and PSP, and these same cell types showed the strongest A152T-specific changes. These findings identify transcriptional alterations that differentiate sporadic AD and sporadic PSP from AD-A152T and PSP-A152T, as well as shared molecular signatures unique to A152T carriers in both PSP and AD. records.summary: Urethral strictures are characterized by fibrotic scar tissue formation in the urethra, leading to difficulties in urination and potential renal dysfunction. records.summary: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are significant neurological complications in elderly surgical patients, yet the underlying immune-mediated mechanisms remain elusive. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption is increasingly recognized as a critical neurovascular event in PND and may result from perioperative immune dysregulation. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of Tregs identified 34 dexmedetomidine-corrected genes, with CTNNB1, encoding β-catenin, emerging as the dominant hub within the protein-protein interaction network. records.title: Mechanisms of risk in pregnancy-associated triple negative breast cancer: insights from spatial omics [2]
records.summary: Pregnancy-associated triple-negative breast cancer (PA-TNBC) is a highly aggressive, hard-to-treat malignancy, with increased risk linked to post-lactational mammary gland involution. To understand this, we used GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler to analyze the transcriptional landscape of 46 treatment-naïve PA-TNBC tissues from 33 women (10 pre-involution/PRE; 23 post-involution/POST, diagnosed within 3 years of delivery), focusing on epithelial and microenvironmental changes. Our findings reveal that the most significant transcriptional differences between PRE and POST exist in non-invasive epithelia and during the transition to invasion. POST non-invasive epithelia showed distinct activation of inflammatory and developmental pathways, while transitioning to TNBC involved elevated chromatin remodeling and migration. Notably, the tumor microenvironment (TME) surrounding POST invasive epithelia featured the greatest immune cell infiltration yet also increased immune exhaustion. Pseudotime analysis highlighted the 1–2 year postpartum window as having the strongest inflammatory signaling. These results underline the need for early molecular detection in normal-appearing post-involution tissues and suggest that targeting the TME is a viable strategy for treating POST PA-TNBC.

records.title: Spatially Decoding Interactypes of Vascular and Synaptic Remodeling in the Glioblastoma Tumor Microenvironment by Surprisal Information-Theoretic Analysis
records.summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly heterogeneous and invasive brain cancer, where interactions between tumor cells, vasculature, and neurons shape disease progression and therapeutic resistance. records.title: TGF-β inhibition ameliorates reactive ALS astrocyte sub-states at single-cell resolution

records.title: Attenuation of DOK3 re-programs tumor-associated macrophages to enhance anti-PD-1-mediated cancer immunotherapy [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: Downstream of Kinase 3 (DOK3) is an adaptor protein that binds and modulates Caspase recruitment domain-containing protein 9 (CARD9) signaling but the role for DOK3 during tumor immune escape remains unclear. Here, we revealed immunosuppressive Osteopontin (SPP1+) tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) to highly express DOK3 while DOK3low/neg TAMs express CARD9 and T cell-homing chemokines within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Interestingly, Dok3-/- mice showed decreased tumor growth and improved response to anti-PD-1 therapy. While DOK3 is constitutively expressed by macrophages, blocking its interaction with CARD9 enhances JNK signaling to reprogram TAMs for improved homing and activation of T cells. Further spatial studies clarified the localization of DOK3high TAMs within the TME and an association of DOK3 expression with progressive disease in an ongoing Phase II study of Lenvatinib/Pembrolizumab in recurrent clear cell gynecological carcinomas. Overall, targeting DOK3-CARD9 axis may represent a new avenue to overcome resistance in cancer immunotherapy by driving the emergence of favorable response-associated TAM states.

records.title: TRIM24 degradation counteracts adaptation to androgen receptor inhibition in prostate cancer [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: The activation of androgen receptor (AR) signaling is the key lineage-specific oncogenic pathway and the primary therapeutic target in prostate cancer. While the therapeutic responses to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (ARSi) are highly variable, disease progression to fatal castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is, in many cases, inevitable. The latter involves processes such as the reactivation of AR signaling, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and the transformation to AR-negative disease through lineage plasticity. In contrast, little is known about the early adaptation mechanisms in residual disease that initiate these processes, leading to tumor relapse. Here, we identify a critical role for TRIM24 in supporting the survival of residual cancer cell subpopulations primed for tumor relapse in vivo. In agreement, the reduction of TRIM24 through bi-functional degraders (dTRIM24) significantly delays or abrogates the emergence of CRPC related to AR-reactivation and lineage plasticity. Mechanistically, dTRIM24 inhibits AR/mTOR signaling in residual disease but, more importantly, also counteracts adaptive pathways directly engaged by AR inhibition, such as STAT3-signaling and the release of EMT-promoting cytokines. records.title: 10x Genomics Visium CytAssist Spatial Gene Expression assay of high-grade serous ovarian cancer for multi-scale integration of histology and gene expression
records.summary: The spatial organization of the tumor microenvironment in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) reflects both tissue morphology and gene expression. We performed 10x Genomics Visium CytAssist spatial transcriptomics on FFPE tissue sections from two HGSOC patients. These data were used to benchmark DiSCoTME, an unsupervised method that integrates histology, gene expression, and spatial context for spatial domain segmentation, against expression-only and image-only approaches. Integrated analysis resolved adjacent tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte-enriched regions and tumor-cell-rich nests that single-modality methods did not separate.

records.title: A comprehensive epithelial and immune characterization of autoimmune gastritis reveals novel aspects of disease pathogenesis
records.summary: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG) is an understudied, adaptive immune-mediated disease characterized by chronic gastric inflammation and autoreactive T and B cells. The epithelial-immune crosstalk leading to a pre-neoplastic environment in AIG is largely unexplored. We profiled the AIG milieu using single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), T cell receptor sequencing (TCR-seq), and flow cytometry from gastric corpus biopsies and peripheral blood of 5 healthy patients and 15 patients with established AIG. Compared to healthy controls, AIG mucosa displayed high-risk, pre-neoplastic transcriptional signatures among distinct epithelial populations. TCR-seq analyses revealed an oligoclonal expansion of CD8+ T cells, a T cell subset that has been assumed to be dispensable in animal models of AIG pathogenesis. We also identified TCR sequences in the peripheral blood of AIG patients that were identical to TCR sequences from patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus, a distinct autoimmune condition that often co-occurs with AIG and related autoimmune endocrinopathies. Finally, our analyses predicted a new antigen whose expression was increased in AIG gastric epithelium. records.title: CDH1 loss remodels gene expression and lineage identity in human mammary epithelial cells [scRNA-Seq]
records.summary: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is a common subtype of breast cancer, molecularly defined by genetic loss of CDH1, and subsequent loss of cell adhesion protein E-cadherin, in ~95% of ILC. Though CDH1 loss occurs early in ILC oncogenesis, it is unclear how this facilitates transformation. We modeled early CDH1 loss using “normal” human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC), i.e. finite lifespan cells reflecting early hyperplasia, and targeted E-cadherin signaling using antibodies versus causing genetic CDH1 loss using siRNA or CRISPR/Cas9-knockout. Transcriptome analysis across four HMEC models showed that the mode of E-cadherin targeting is critical for the subsequent phenotype. Antibody-mediated inhibition of cell-cell contacts induced gene signatures of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), consistent with the role of E-cadherin suppression during the EMT process. Conversely, genetic CDH1 loss – as in ILC oncogenesis – repressed EMT signatures, and instead remodeled gene expression toward a luminal epithelial phenotype. RNA-seq, single cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, microscopy, and ATACseq analyses support that CDH1 loss induces lineage remodeling to a luminal state, which is mirrored in transcriptomic analysis of clinical ILC precursor lesions. records.title: Conserved cell state dynamics reveal targetable resistance patterns in ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma
records.summary: We characterized how the cell states of normal FTE are transformed into intra-tumoral heterogeneity in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC) using single-cell transcriptomics of treatment-naive tumors and normal FTE. records.title: Targeting the 9p24.1 Axis with JAK Inhibition and Immune Checkpoint Blockade in Lymphomas
records.summary: Amplification of chromosome 9p24.1 drives coordinated upregulation of JAK–STAT signaling and the immune checkpoint ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, promoting lymphoma cell survival and immune evasion. While PD-1 blockade demonstrates substantial activity in 9p24.1-spectrum lymphomas, responses remain incomplete, particularly outside classical Hodgkin lymphoma. We hypothesized that dual targeting of the 9p24.1 axis through JAK1/2 inhibition could enhance immune checkpoint blockade by simultaneously disrupting tumor-intrinsic survival signaling and reprogramming the tumor microenvironment. Using 9p24.1-amplified lymphoma cell lines, bulk RNA sequencing, a three-dimensional immune co-culture organoid platform, ex vivo patient peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and complementary syngeneic and humanized murine models, the effects of ruxolitinib alone and in combination with pembrolizumab were evaluated. Ruxolitinib preferentially reduced PD-L1/PD-L2 and c-MYC expression in 9p24.1-amplified cell lines and induced transcriptional upregulation of antigen presentation pathways, including MHC class II–associated genes. In organoid co-culture systems, combination therapy enhanced CD3⁺ T cell tumor infiltration and increased tumor cell apoptosis compared with monotherapy. Within the peripheral immu
evidence: In vivo, combination therapy suppressed tumor growth, prolonged survival, and was accompanied by increased intratumoral T cell activation, findings corroborated in spatial CosMx protein tissue microarray analysis.

records.title: Morphology–Molecular Alignment Profiling: integrating mitochondrial morphology with single-cell gene programs in human neurons
records.summary: Mitochondrial morphology is linked to neuronal state. However, organelle phenotypes are rarely co-quantified with cell-resolved transcriptomes in human neurons. Here, we introduce Morphology–Molecular Alignment Profiling (MORPH–MAP), a framework combining mitochondrial imaging with Xenium in situ transcriptomics in human iPSC-derived neural cells. By mapping TOMM20-based morphology metrics and transcripts profiles to one-to-one cell identities, MORPH–MAP enables integrated analysis of mitochondrial morphology and molecular programs across cell types and differentiation states within the same culture. As a proof of concept, we applied MORPH–MAP to dopaminergic-lineage cells derived from Rett syndrome patients and healthy controls, identifying DNA damage-response pathways linked to mitochondrial morphology, with a p53–p21 stress program emerging during differentiation. Pharmacological p21 attenuation with UC2288 partially shifted mitochondrial morphology in patients toward a control-like state and ameliorated MAP2-positive dendritic phenotypes. Together, MORPH–MAP provides an approach for linking organelle morphology with molecular states across development and disease.
evidence: Here, we introduce Morphology–Molecular Alignment Profiling (MORPH–MAP), a framework combining mitochondrial imaging with Xenium in situ transcriptomics in human iPSC-derived neural cells.

records.title: Endothelial Matrin-3 Limits Cellular Senescence and Lipid Dysregulation to Protect Against Murine Atherosclerosis [RNA-Seq HCAEC]
records.summary: Matrin-3 is a DNA- and RNA-binding protein, and its disruption in mice and humans is associated with bicuspid aortic valve, aortic coarctation and patent ductus arteriosus. However, the role of endothelial matrin-3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, bulk RNA-sequencing identified hundreds of differentially expressed in human endothelial cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that the enriched pathways relate to DNA replication, p53 signaling, cell cycle, and cellular senescence. Single-nucleus RNA-seq revealed that endothelial matrin-3 deficiency impairs signaling and promotes inflammation in hepatocytes. Finally, matrin-3 expression was reduced in mouse and human atherosclerotic plaques. records.summary: PARP inhibitor (PARPi) efficacy in BRCA-mutant breast cancer is driven by DNA damage-induced synthetic lethality and immune activation, supporting combination with immune checkpoint blockade. In the TALAVE study, patients with advanced BRCA-mutant or wild-type (WT) HER2-negative breast cancer received talazoparib followed by talazoparib plus avelumab. records.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of a rare case of rhabdoid carcinoma of the pancreas [CosMx]
records.summary: Undifferentiated carcinoma of the pancreas with rhabdoid features is a rare and lethal variant, comprising only 2-7 percent of all pancreas cancer cases. Here we present a single patient case with in-depth molecular characterization, including whole exome DNA sequencing as well as GeoMx/CosMx spatial transcriptome profiling. DNA mutational analyses indicate this case possessed wild-type KRAS and intact SMARCB1/INI1, both of which are typically mutated in pancreas cancers and those with rhabdoid features. OncoKB gene panel analysis revealed loss-of-function mutations in TP53, KMT2C, KMT2D, and a gain-of-function in BRAF. This mutational profile has not been previously reported in this rare variant of pancreas cancer. Spatial RNA analyses of tumor sections and adjacent pancreas reveal transcriptionally distinct tumor cell types, and distinct cell types in adjacent tissues. The unique transcriptomic features and mutational profile of this case highlights the heterogeneity of pancreas cancers, even within rare variants, highlighting the need for early genomic profiling to identify actionable mutations such as BRAF that may respond to targeted therapies.

records.title: Performance of the 10X Genomics Flex Single-Cell Sequencing Assay and its Application to Overcome Challenges in Clinical Trial Samples
records.summary: Background: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has become essential for understanding disease biology, yet its application in clinical trials is often limited by logistical challenges associated with the handling of biospecimens. Newly developed protocols aim to address these limitations by enabling profiling of fixed tissue. These new solutions need to be benchmarked against well-established protocols to assess their performance and suitability for clinical research. Results: In the present study we systematically compared different fixed-tissue and nuclei-based RNA-sequencing workflows in a set of solid tumor samples, which were collected and preserved following common procedures in clinical trials. When applied to both frozen tumor tissue and FFPE blocks, the 10X Genomics GEM-X Flex Gene Expression assay, in combination with the "chop-fix" preprocessing protocol, demonstrated enhanced data quality - characterized by higher gene and UMI detection sensitivity and slightly reduced ambient RNA background - relative to the standard GEM-X Universal Gene Expression solution. Furthermore, this protocol improved the capture of specific biological signals and resolved cell states that were less distinct with conventional approaches. records.title: Genomic and epigenomic insights into purkinje and granule neurons in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia using single-nucleus multiome analysis
records.summary: Although the human cerebellum is known to be neuropathologically impaired in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD), the cell type-specific transcriptional and epigenomic changes that contribute to this pathology are not well understood. Here, we report single-nucleus multiome (snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both cerebellum (n = 9) and frontal cortex (n = 6) of AD/ADRD patients and normal controls (n = 8). Using peak-to-gene linkage analysis, we identified 431,834 significant linkages between gene expression and cell subtype-specific chromatin accessibility regions enriched for candidate cis-regulatory elements (cCREs). These cCREs were associated with AD/ADRD-specific transcriptomic changes and disease-related gene regulatory networks. Differential trajectory analysis revealed disease-associated genes in granule populations in AD/ADRD cerebellum, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrative analysis of snATAC-seq-derived cCREs, genome-wide AD/ADRD GWAS loci, and three-dimensional (3D) genome data pinpointed two likely causal SNPs, including rs4788201 linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells, and rs62056801 linked to KANSL1 in granule cells. records.title: Immune and Cellular Determinants of Response to HMA-Venetoclax Regimens in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
records.summary: Hypomethylating agents (HMAs) combined with Venetoclax have redefined the therapeutic landscape of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), yet the biological underpinnings of treatment response remain elusive. We integrated clinical and genomic profiling in 132 patients with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory AML treated with HMA-Venetoclax. Additionally, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing and T cell receptor (TCR) profiling at baseline and after one cycle in 10 newly diagnosed cases to dissect cell-intrinsic and immune determinants of response. Response rates and overall survival were consistent with published data, supporting HMA-Venetoclax as a valid bridge to transplant. Targeted next-generation sequencing delineated molecular subgroups, confirming the favorable impact of IDH2 and the poor prognosis associated with TP53 mutations. scRNAseq and TCR analysis revealed novel immune correlates: responders showed expansion of cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells, increased TCR clonality, and activation of inflammatory and antigen presentation pathways. Non-responders exhibited baseline inflammatory signaling (Interferon, NF-κB), impaired myeloid maturation via NOTCH and RAS, and a suppressive microenvironment enriched in IDO1⁺ regulatory dendritic cells. records.title: Longitudinal multi-region proteomics reveals preferential inflammatory-matrix remodeling at the infiltrative edge during glioma progression
records.summary: Purpose: The infiltrative edge is a potential source of residual glioma, but its molecular evolution relative to the tumor core remains unclear. We investigated regional proteomic changes during malignant histological progression and evaluated a candidate associated with recurrent-edge remodeling. Experimental Design: We profiled 102 FFPE specimens, comprising 60 tumor-core, 27 infiltrative-edge, and 15 brain-reference tissues, in a study of 29 longitudinally sampled patients with diffuse glioma (19 IDH-mutant and 10 IDH-wild-type). Proteomic programs were evaluated using independent proteomic and single-cell cohorts, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. SERPINH1 was tested by prophylactic self-amplifying mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (sa-mRNA-LNP) immunization before orthotopic GL261-Luc implantation. Results: Proteomic analysis identified a continuous synaptic–neuronal to inflammatory–matrix remodeling (SYN–IMR) axis. Matched tumor cores shifted toward IMR at recurrence (mean ΔSSIprog, −1.206; P = 0.014), with a concordant change in an independent cohort (−0.561; P = 0.042). records.title: Circulating pre-osteoclasts are primed for osteoclast fate and synovial tissue homing in psoriatic arthritis
records.summary: We performed imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (10x Genomics Xenium) on synovial tissue from near-healthy and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) donors. Each donor received autologous radiolabelled monocytes 24 hours before biopsy. Sections were profiled with the Xenium Prime 5K Human Pan-tissue and Pathways panel plus a 50-gene custom add-on. The add-on targets synovial, tissue-homing and osteoclastogenesis genes. The data characterise the spatial organisation of synovial cell populations, including monocyte-derived and osteoclast-lineage cells, in PsA compared with near-healthy synovium.

records.title: Circulating pre-osteoclasts are primed for osteoclast fate and synovial tissue homing in psoriatic arthritis [Parse scRNA-seq]
records.summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of synovial tissue from psoriatic arthritis patients using Parse Evercode platform. Fresh whole synovium was digested into single cell suspension, whole live synovial cells FACS-sorted, then fixed-permeabilised per Parse Evercode V2.1.1 protocol (quarter buffer volumes after discussion with Parse scientists). Three samples (hvsyn019, hvsyn021, psab05) were pooled and processed across 8 sublibraries, then computationally demultiplexed. Sequencing performed on Illumina NovaSeq X Plus. Quality-control and alignment completed using Parse split-pipe software with GRCh38 genome (Ensembl v111). Cells filtered if >3 MAD from median library size/gene count or >25% mitochondrial genes.

records.title: A Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Atlas Characterising Transcriptional and Immune Diversity in Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas
records.summary: Adult-type diffuse gliomas are defined by the IDH axis, yet how this biology constrains malignant cell-state repertoires and their immune-modulatory potential remains unclear. We profiled 69 tumours using scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics, and resolved seven recurrent malignant cell states: astrocyte-like progenitor cells (ALPC), hypoxia, cycling G1/S, cycling G2/M, oligo-lineage, neuro-oligo-lineage, and neuro-lineage. The IDH axis strongly biased state occupancy and malignant–immune composition, with IDH-mutant tumours dominated by differentiated lineage-like states and relative immune paucity, whereas glioblastoma (GBM) showed expansion of ALPC and hypoxia states alongside increased myeloid and lymphoid infiltration. Orthogonal analyses supported that ALPC-associated markers are expressed in situ and in patient-derived stem-permissive cultures, consistent with a stem-like, differentiation-competent malignant phenotype. State-resolved pathway analysis identified mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation programs enriched in GBM ALPC and extracellular matrix remodelling, and chemotaxis-associated programs enriched in GBM hypoxia. records.title: An attention-based framework for interpretation of cell-cell interactions from spatial transcriptomics
records.summary: Spatial transcriptomic data enable study of cell-cell communication, yet current tools lack dynamic, interpretable estimates and spatial range of interactions. We present AMICI, an interpretable attention framework that estimates effective pairwise interaction radii, resolves sender-receiver subpopulations, and links communication to gene programs. AMICI recovers ground-truth interactions in semi-synthetic data, uncovers communication programs in mouse cortex, and reveals tumor-immune associations linked to ER programs in breast cancer. To test whether AMICI generalizes beyond the tumor microenvironment to a tissue with well-characterized multicellular organization profiled with a different spatial technology, we applied AMICI to a human tonsil spatial transcriptomics dataset profiled with the CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (1,000-gene panel), which is provided in this submission. AMICI recovered an interaction network consistent with known lymphoid anatomy, including germinal center (follicular dendritic cell, GC B cell, Tfh cell) and fibroblast-CD4 T cell zone programs.
evidence: An attention-based framework for interpretation of cell-cell interactions from spatial transcriptomics.

records.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex
records.summary: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) are common neuropsychiatric conditions with complex etiology and heterogenous presentation. The cellular mechanisms underlying MDD and BD have expanded beyond the monoamine hypothesis and abundant evidence links dysregulated circuit activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) to both MDD and BD. The laminar organization of dlPFC circuits was captured in this study using the 10x Genomics Visium platform to generate spatial RNA-sequencing data in postmortem tissue from adult human brain donors (N=119). We investigated sex-specific gene expression changes associated with MDD and BD in the context of the dlPFC cortical layers to identify converging and unique molecular signatures of each disorder. In MDD females and BD males and females, we identified elevated expression of genes related to cellular responses to inflammation, hypoxia, and blood-brain-barrier integrity and decreased expression of neuropeptide modulators of neuronal activity. Domain-restricted comparisons confirmed that the increased pro-inflammatory signature was present throughout the dlPFC tissue section, and not limited to domains enriched in blood vessels, astrocytes, and microglia. records.title: Human microglia remove intraneuronal a-synuclein aggregates in a stem cell model of Parkinson’s disease [scRNA-Seq]
records.summary: Microglia are the primary immune cells of the brain but their role in Parkinson’s disease is not fully understood. Although most studies suggest that chronic microglial activation is toxic to neurons, they also exert beneficial functions in the early stages of neuronal pathology that are not yet well defined. We used iPSC modelling to investigate how human microglia respond to α-synuclein aggregation that forms de novo in human dopaminergic neurons with α-synuclein gene triplication or is triggered by fibrils. We found that microglia cleared Ser129 phosphorylated α-synuclein aggregates without exacerbating neurotoxicity, using a contact-dependent mechanism involving selective phagocytosis (i.e. trogocytosis) of neuronal sub-compartments that is independent of TREM2 or phosphotidylserine. In the presence of intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates, microglia exhibited morphological changes and transcriptomic profiles indicative of activation. Using single cell sequencing, we identified a sub-cluster of disease-associated microglia (DAM) in association with this phenotype, and GPNMB as a key effector of a-synuclein aggregate clearance by microglial lysosomes. records.title: Heatstroke induces immunosuppression through expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and IL-10-mediated impairment of T cell cytotoxicity [scRNA-Seq]

Disease progression was characterized by elevated levels of damage-associated molecules (e.g., S100A8/A12) and immunosuppressive molecules (e.g., IL-10), accompanied by a reduction in the expression of T cell- and HLA-associated genes.
