records.title: Highly efficient organoid-derived cyst cultures as a drug discovery platform for polycystic kidney disease
records.summary: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) causes the slow, progressive formation of fluid-filled cysts within the kidney that ultimately leads to renal failure. Despite being the most common genetic kidney disease, therapies for ADPKD are limited. Ureteric bud (UB) organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC) have been developed to model ADPKD. Here, we describe a protocol to generate UB organoids in large-scale suspension culture that is amenable to drug discovery. Day 12 nephron organoids grown from wildtype and PKD2-deficient hiPSC lines were transdifferentiated into UB organoids. Wildtype and cyst-forming PKD2-deficient UB organoids were characterized by immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR and single cell RNA-seq. Compound screening for cyst reduction was performed over 10 days, and cyst numbers and diameters were measured from brightfield images. Our protocol for generating UB organoids is highly scalable, with up to 2000 organoids forming from ~50 nephron organoids in 7 days. The UB organoids develop characteristic tubular extensions and express UB-specific markers, including AQP2, WNT9B and KRT8. records.title: Engineered in vitro microvascular model of the blood-brain-tumor barrier to probe vascular biology of pediatric diffuse midline glioma
records.summary: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor that is difficult to treat because the blood-brain-tumor barrier (BBTB) prevents most drugs from reaching the tumor. A major obstacle for understanding this tumor-vascular niche is the lack of a perfusable vascular model of DMG. To address this, we have established an in vitro model of the DMG-BBTB, comprised of a co-culture of patient-derived DMG tumor cells, primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells, astrocytes, and vascular pericytes, embedded in a fibrin matrix within a microfluidic chip. We report the development and characterization of self-assembled microvascular networks, with consistent vasculature development across a range of tumor cell densities. Perfusion studies showed no significant alterations in vascular permeability when tumor cells were present. To elucidate transcriptomic changes, we employed scRNAseq on devices containing BBB, DMG-BBTB, or tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα)-stimulated control. We observed significant differential gene expression between BBB and DMG-BBTB, distinct from inflammatory signatures seen with TNFα perturbation. records.title: Dysregulation of mechanosensing signaling in monocytes of patients with systemic sclerosis is associated with skin inflammation
records.summary: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a life threatening autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Fibrosis is driven in part by infiltration of immune cells, including monocytes that become chronically activated within fibrotic tissue. Although monocytes infiltrate the skin and contribute to tissue repair and fibrosis, how the mechanical properties of fibrotic skin regulate their function remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that increased skin stiffness directly controls human monocyte activation through mechanosensing. Re analysis of single cell RNA sequencing datasets revealed that skin infiltrating monocytes exhibit heightened inflammatory signatures compared to circulating counterparts, with further amplification in SSc. Using collagen coated hydrogels modeling physiologic and fibrotic stiffness, we show that increased stiffness induces secretion of IL 1β, TNF, and IL 6, enhances CD86 expression, and broadly upregulates inflammatory transcriptional programs while suppressing anti inflammatory pathways. Mechanistically, stiffness driven activation was associated with chromatin remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming, identifying the transcription factor SP1 as a central regulator. records.title: Transitions between cancer stem cells and non-cancer stem cells during metastasis
records.summary: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) and non-cancer stem cells (nCSCs) exhibit dynamic bidirectional transitions during metastasis, yet the mechanisms and therapeutic implications of this interconversion remain poorly understood. To investigate these transitions and their therapeutic relevance, we establish four orthotopic breast cancer mouse models using stable lineage labeling: CSC-alone, nCSC-alone, bilateral CSC/nCSC, and mixed CSC/nCSC tumors. Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence analyses support bidirectional phenotypic interconversion between both CSC- and nCSC- derived populations during tumor progression and metastasis, with nCSCs acquiring CD24-high CSC-like states and CSCs adopting EGFR-high nCSC-like phenotypes in both primary tumors and metastatic lesions. Monotherapies targeting CD24 with ATG-031 or EGFR with osimertinib produce only partial inhibition of tumor growth and metastasis, consistent with the possibility that cellular plasticity may provide an escape route from targeting a single state. records.title: Multiomic Profiling of 85 iPSC Lines from Familial Dementia Reveals Cellular Diversity and Regulators of Organoid Development [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: Systematic molecular characterization of human iPSC lines carrying disease-associated mutations is needed to distinguish disease-related biology from variation in cell state, genomic integrity, and genome-editing history; yet such systematic characterization is uncommon. Here we profiled 85 human iPSC lines carrying MAPT mutations and isogenic controls using whole-genome sequencing, long-read sequencing of the MAPT locus, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, and DNA methylation arrays. Single-cell analyses identified four reproducible iPSC states and candidate surface markers for their isolation. Whole genome sequencing revealed unintended editing events and recurrent 20q11.21 duplications, which was associated with increased ID1 expression and impaired cortical organoid patterning. Transcriptomic analyses identified pathways associated with organoid quality and changes linked to clonal selection and editing, underscoring the need to use unconverted lines as isogenic controls. By providing an in-depth genomic characterization of MAPT iPSCs, this dataset serves as a proof of principle to enhance iPSC utility in biological research.

records.title: Targeted Insertion of Corrective CFTR Transgene Replicates Native Expression Pattern with Functional Restoration in Cystic Fibrosis Airway Epithelium
records.summary: Our objective is to develop a universal gene editing therapeutic for individuals with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). Because of the large number of CFTR variants, we sought to develop a mutation-agnostic methodology capable of efficient CFTR2-27 integration into CFTR intron 1. Following electroporation of CF primary airway basal stem cells with intron 1-targeted Cas9/gRNA, we delivered CFTR2-27 donor, flanked by a splice acceptor and polyadenylation signal, via integrase defective lentivirus vector. Molecular characterization revealed highly efficient integration of CFTR2-27 into the native CFTR intron 1 with most insertion events reflecting the desired homology directed repair. Integration resulted in functional restoration of CFTR channel activity in fully differentiated airway epithelium with significant improvement of mucus hydration and transport. ATAC-seq revealed that the native CFTR chromatin architecture was unaffected by the CFTR2-27 insertion and importantly, scRNA-seq demonstrated that the cell type-specific expression of the introduced transgene replicated that of the endogenous CFTR.

records.title: Mapping the Tissue Architecture and Endothelial-PEC Network in Hepatic Angiomyolipoma Using Single-cell and Spatial Transcriptomics [Spatial Transcriptomics]
records.summary: Hepatic angiomyolipoma is a rare mesenchymal tumor frequently associated with tuberous sclerosis complex gene mutations. The tumor microenvironment profiling enables the discovery of potential therapeutic targets. Here, we proﬁle 18,214 cells from tumor and adjacent tissues to identify distinct cell subsets, validate perivascular epithelioid cell biomarkers, predict cellular origins, and characterize molecular networks. Complementarily, we applied microarray-based spatial transcriptomics to map tissue architecture on three hepatic angiomyolipoma specimens by spot arrays. Tumor and normal regions were annotated using robust cell type decomposition and multimodal intersection analysis, integrating snRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data. We demonstrate that the perivascular epithelioid cell share substantial transcriptional similarity with endothelial cells and and show a continuous differentiation trajectory. This interaction might be regulated by PDGFD-PDGFRB signaling promotes autophagy by activating the Ras pathway potentially contributing to the pathogenesis and progression of hepatic angiomyolipoma. Our results provide a potential therapeutic strategy by disrupting perivascular epithelioid cell and endothelial cells interaction to improve therapeutic effect.

records.overall_design: This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach to characterize the cellular and spatial landscape of hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML). Fresh tumor and paired normal tissues from one patient were processed for single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) using the 10x Genomics platform. For spatial transcriptomics (ST), FFPE sections from three HAML specimens were mounted on Visium slides, processed for H&E staining, and sequenced to generate spatially resolved gene expression profiles. snRNA-seq data were quality-controlled and clustered using Seurat, with cell types annotated via canonical markers and SingleR. ST data were analyzed with SpaceRanger and Seurat, and cell-type deconvolution was performed using Robust Cell Type Decomposition (RCTD) and Multimodal Intersection Analysis (MIA) to map snRNA-seq-defined populations onto tissue sections. PEC characterization included differential expression, pseudotime trajectory (Monocle2), transcription factor regulatory network (SCENIC), and copy number variation (InferCNV) analyses. Cell–cell communication was inferred using CellChat. Validation experiments included immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and western blotting for selected markers and signaling pathways in paired tumor and normal tissues.

records.title: Cytotoxic T cell derived IFNγ mediates placental immune dysregulation in villitis of unknown etiology
records.summary: Villitis of unknown etiology (VUE) is a common chronic inflammatory placental lesion associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, yet the immunological drivers of sustained placental injury remain undefined. Here, we identify interferon gamma (IFNγ)-driven immune dysregulation as a central feature of VUE. Spatial transcriptomic profiling revealed a coordinated IFNγ-associated inflammatory program across decidual stromal cells (DSC), trophoblasts, and infiltrating immune populations. Multiplexed in situ analyses identified that infiltrating cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, including a CD11c+ effector subset, are a significant source of IFNγ within VUE lesions. Functional studies demonstrated that IFNγ reprograms normally tolerogenic DSCs and trophoblasts to upregulate major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and II molecules and increase production of the T cell recruiting chemokine C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10). Sustained IFNγ signaling further disrupted decidual functional programs while reinforcing chemokine-mediated immune cell recruitment. Together, these findings define a feed forward inflammatory circuit in which IFNγ producing cytotoxic T cells undermine placental immune tolerance and perpetuate villous injury in VUE.
evidence: Spatial transcriptomic profiling revealed a coordinated IFNγ-associated inflammatory program across decidual stromal cells (DSC), trophoblasts, and infiltrating immune populations.

records.title: Single-cell profiling of limbic excitatory neurons reveals dysregulation of metabolic pathways in Parkinson’s disease
records.summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common age-related neurodegenerative disorder that is pathologically characterized by the presence of Lewy bodies within neurons across several brain regions. Although the severe, selective degeneration of pigmented dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain results in a characteristic constellation of motor symptoms, how additional neuronal populations are affected in disease and contribute to neuropsychiatric symptoms remains unclear. The amygdala is one of the most frequent brain regions to harbor Lewy bodies in both PD and Alzheimer’s disease with co-existing alpha-synuclein pathology. To understand how neurons and glial cells are altered in this subcortical limbic area in PD, we performed single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) of patients and age-matched controls that yielded 168,270 transcriptomes. Following stringent quality control measures, we observed increased microglia with shifts towards activated states in disease. Furthermore, we found transcriptional perturbations of genes linked to metabolic pathways in excitatory neurons, including upregulation of TFEB, though not in inhibitory neurons. records.summary: Keratin-positive giant cell-rich tumor (KPGCT) is a newly described bone and soft tissue tumor. records.title: Chromosome 6q mediated loss of LATS1 tumour suppression as a targetable mechanism of ultra-high-risk posterior fossa A ependymoma [Xenium]
records.summary: Posterior fossa A (PFA) ependymoma is the most common and lethal paediatric ependymoma subgroup, with relapse remaining almost uniformly fatal. Our study reveals that loss of chromosome 6q is among the most common copy number variants observed in PFA deaths and explores the biological mechanisms underlying this loss. We identify LATS1 loss as a defining feature of 6q-deleted PFA ependymoma, leading to Hippo pathway dysregulation and activation of YAP/TEAD signalling. These findings uncover a previously unrecognised molecular driver of PFA tumour aggressiveness and establish a mechanistic rationale for targeting Hippo pathway components in this disease.

records.title: Inference and validation of causal genetic interactions in aging human fibroblasts
records.summary: In the past hundred years, the fraction of fatalities due to age-related disease has risen from an envied minority of cases to the leading cause of death and economic morbidity in the developed world. Despite notable advances in understanding aging, its intrinsic complexity has prevented major therapeutic breakthroughs. This complexity extends across all systems and scales in an organism, leaving a ‘fingerprint of aging’ across every aspect of cell and tissue behavior whose interrelationships are difficult to untangle. records.title: scRNA-seq of PBMC from patients with anterior STEMI reveals a monocyte-derived population enriched for platelet-related transcripts in patients with intramyocardial haemorrhage
records.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) was conducted 24 hours after treatment in patients anterior ST-segment–elevation on myocardial infarction (STEMI) receiving either placebo or the CX3CR1 antagonist KAND567 (n=8 per group). Differential expression analysis identified pro-platelet basic protein (PPBP) and platelet factor 4 (PF4), both platelet-related chemokines, among the top three upregulated genes in the placebo group, but absent in the KAND567 group. Within the placebo arm, stratification by presence of intramyocardial haemorrhage (IMH) revealed PPBP and PF4 as the top two genes significantly upregulated in IMH-positive participants. records.title: Single-cell transcriptomics of peripheral blood reveals race-associated gene expression divergence in breast cancer from precancerous stages
records.summary: Black women more likely develop breast cancer at younger ages compared with other populations, yet reasons behind are not fully understood. As the immune system influences cancer development and progression, we hypothesized that immune differences by race could reflect underlying mechanisms. Here, we developed a single-cell transcriptomic PBMC atlas, including samples from Non-Hispanic Black patients with high-risk breast lesions, DCIS, and invasive breast cancer and compared them with Non-Hispanic White patients. PBMC composition varied modestly by disease state and race, whereas transcriptomic divergence was pronounced. Differential expression analysis showed that transcriptomic diverges in invasive disease from precancer states, and that race-associated transcriptomic difference was also strongest in invasive breast cancer. Covarying neighborhood analysis and pathway analysis identified race/ethnicity-associated pathways enriched in NHB, featuring pathways linked to chronic inflammation, immune suppression, and immune aging in monocytes, dendritic cells, CD4+ T cells, and B cells. This dataset is a valuable resource characterizing peripheral immune changes during breast cancer development from racially/ethnically inclusive populations.

records.title: Plasticity of Human Microglia and Brain Perivascular Macrophages in Aging and Alzheimer’s Disease
records.summary: The complex roles of myeloid cells, including microglia and perivascular macrophages, are central to the neurobiology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet they remain incompletely understood. records.summary: Although immune-checkpoint blockade therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment, many patients fail to respond, highlighting the need to identify predictive biomarkers and target mechanisms that limit treatment efficacy. Here, we investigated the mechanisms underlying resistance to atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo/Bev) therapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We profiled tumor ecosystems using single-cell RNA sequencing and mass cytometry by time-of-flight from a cohort of patients with advanced HCC receiving Atezo/Bev, integrating these data with external single-cell datasets. records.title: Cellular and Transcriptional Landscape of Human Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
records.summary: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a congenital heart defect characterized by impaired development of the left ventricle, often managed through surgical palliation creating a single ventricle (SV). Failure of the anatomical right ventricle (RV) represents a common complication with high mortality. We used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to generate a map of the pediatric non-failing (NF) and failing (SysHF) SV. Fibroblasts and endocardial cells displayed the greatest transcriptional shifts between NF and SysHF. Notably, activated fibroblasts expanded in SysHF, and endocardial cells demonstrated a pro-fibrotic shift in SysHF samples. Ligand-target analysis predicted disease-state specific signaling from CCN2 expressing endocardial cells to fibroblasts in SysHF. In silico perturbation predicted FOS and JUN as regulators of fibroblast activation and endocardial pathogenesis. Finally, HLHS data was compared to adult human and murine RV failure to gain insight into shared pathological processes and the suitability of current animal models. These findings provide a foundational reference of SV and implicate cell non-autonomous signaling between endocardial cells and fibroblasts as drivers of SV systolic heart failure.
evidence: We used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to generate a map of the pediatric non-failing (NF) and failing (SysHF) SV.

records.title: HypoAD: volumetric and single-cell analysis reveals changes in the human hypothalamus in aging and Alzheimer's disease
records.summary: Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms, and neuroendocrine processes are key features of aging and neurodegeneration. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human aging and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here, we present HypoAD, a comprehensive atlas of the human hypothalamus in aging and AD, integrating high-resolution MRI from 202 individuals with single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) of 614,403 nuclei from young, AD, and age-matched non-dementia controls. Our analysis reveals that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress, and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, exhibiting significant changes in both volumes and gene expression during aging and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. records.title: Overcoming senescence to engineer scalable universal T cell therapies [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: Adoptive cell therapies have been transformative for some patients with cancer. Autologous cell therapies face many challenges, establishing the need for allogeneic strategies. However, cellular senescence limits lymphocyte proliferation and functionality, constraining our ability to produce scalable allogeneic solutions to increase patient access. Ex vivo activation of T or NK cells accelerates this process, curtailing expansion and effector capacity. To address this, we integrated insights from T cell lymphoproliferative diseases, leukemic T cell lines, genome-wide CRISPR screens, and transgene enrichment screens and developed a genetic editing strategy targeting replicative senescence-related genes. Applied to healthy donor CD8+ T cells, this editing strategy enabled quintillion-fold ex vivo expansion while preserving effector function and fundamental lymphocyte attributes. Further engineering, introducing a CAR transgene and histocompatibility edits, potentiated production of thousands of “Universal Effector Cell” (UEC) doses from a single donor. UECs offer a scalable, off-the-shelf cell therapy platform, delivering potent, functional therapeutics and improving patient access. records.title: Translational profiling of ET-insensitive cell populations in ER+ breast cancer reveals new therapeutic vulnerabilities [scRNA-Seq]
records.summary: Endocrine therapy resistance in ER+ breast cancer remains a major therapeutic challenge in clinic. This study offers a robust workflow to identify ET-insensitive cell populations that persist under selective pressure of ET in clinical samples and experimental models. We demonstrated that these populations are transcriptionally diverse and not defined by ER status/activity or molecular subtype. Importantly, we developed a predictive therapeutic pipeline that enables identification of new drugs tailored to target ET-insensitive cell populations. These findings provide a clinically relevant strategy for overcoming ET resistance and support the integration of single-cell profiling and organoid modeling into precision oncology workflows.

records.title: Single cell transcriptomic atlas of patient bone marrow biopsies after anti-BCMA CAR T cell therapy [scRNA-Seq]
records.summary: CAR-T cell therapy is an effective treatment for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. However, this treatment has been linked to a number of potentially fatal adverse events with incompletely understood biological underpinnings. These events include a failure of bone marrow (BM) regeneration, which leads to dysfunctional hematopoiesis, a condition also referred to as immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT). To address this issue, we analyzed BM core biopsies of CAR-T cell treated patients (N=24) by combining single-cell RNA-sequencing with single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics. Focusing on patients with ICAHT (N=10), our analysis revealed hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) niche alterations towards a cellular network around inflamed mesenchymal cells that relay IFN- signaling from T cells to monocytes. Monocytes in turn provide pro-inflammatory feedback to mesenchymal cells through IL1B signaling. HSCs from cytopenic patients exposed to this niche up-regulate a senescence signature, indicating a cause of dysfunctional hematopoiesis. Our study deciphers a BM niche interaction network that maintains prolonged inflammation and impairs bone marrow regeneration by inducing HSC senescence.

records.title: Spatial transcriptomic atlas of patient bone marrow biopsies after anti-BCMA CAR T cell therapy [Xenium]
records.summary: Anti-BCMA CAR-T cell therapy is an efficient treatment strategy for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Nevertheless, a set of potentially fatal adverse events has been linked to this treatment, including immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT), a condition with largely unknown biological underpinnings. To address this issue, we analyzed bone marrow (BM) core biopsies of anti-BCMA CAR-T cell treated patients at spatial single-cell resolution by combining single-cell RNA-sequencing with spatial transcriptomics by in situ sequencing. Focusing on patients with sustained ICAHT, our integrated analysis strategy revealed an inflammatory mesenchymal cell population, serving as the signaling hub to relay inflammatory signaling to monocytes within the BM, which we validated in vitro. HSCs from cytopenic patients up-regulated a senescence signature, indicating a putative cause of perturbed hematopoiesis. Our study deciphers a mechanism to maintain prolonged inflammation of the BM microenvironment and suggests that this inflammatory state may underlie ICAHT by inducing HSC senescence.

records.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood immune cells in type 2 diabetes
records.summary: RNA-seq of coding RNA from single cells Single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood immune cells from individuals who were apparently healthy or had type 2 diabetes (T2D), generated to test whether the circulating immune compartment is transcriptionally altered in T2D. Peripheral blood leukocytes from two healthy and two T2D donors were profiled. Cells were captured and barcoded on the BD Rhapsody single-cell platform with sample-tag multiplexing, and whole-transcriptome libraries were prepared together with an antibody-derived tag (AbSeq) library. Following demultiplexing, quality control, normalisation, and integration, cells were annotated to major circulating immune populations and compared between conditions. The analysis identified neutrophils as the most transcriptionally altered compartment in T2D. These samples were generated as part of a larger multiplexed sequencing run; the processed data for the remaining samples belong to a separate ongoing study and will be deposited on publication of that work.

records.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Across Populations With Perianal Fistulizing Crohn’s Disease Shows Proinflammatory CD4+ Macrophage Involvement in Disease Progression
records.summary: Background and aims: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (CD) is a severe complication associated with altered immune and tissue responses. This study aimed to identify cellular and molecular features distinguishing inflamed rectal CD with and without fistula across African American (AA) and European American (EA) populations. Results: Single-cell sequencing of 262,000 rectal mucosal cells revealed reduced phagocytic and antigen-processing signatures in CD4⁺CD68⁺ macrophages from fistulizing CD. These macrophages formed large aggregates near epithelial crypts and altered local cellular signaling networks. The strongest cellular pathway differences occurred between AA and EA patients with fistulizing disease and between fistulizing and non-fistulizing CD among AA patients. Conclusion: CD4⁺ macrophage aggregation and altered immune-cell interactions may contribute to the severe inflammation underlying perianal fistula formation and progression, with population-specific differences potentially influencing disease severity.

records.title: Ultrasound-Mediated BBB Opening Promotes Microglial Reprogramming and Enhanced Endothelial Interactions in the Human Peritumoral Brain [scRNA-Seq]
records.summary: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) restricts entry of therapeutics and shapes immune surveillance in the central nervous system, while microglia maintain barrier integrity and coordinate repair. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound with intravenously administered microbubbles (LIPU/MB) transiently opens the BBB in patients, with restoration mostly occurring within about an hour; however, how microglia respond to LIPU/MB during this acute repair window in the human brain remains unknown. We report on intraoperative LIPU/MB studies where the peritumoral brain of glioblastoma patients was biopsied 45 minutes after sonication and analyzed, as part of phase I/II clinical trials (NCT04528680). We integrated single-cell RNA-seq, single-cell ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. We observe that LIPU/MB modulates perivascular microglia by promoting extension of processes toward the endothelium, inducing pro-inflammatory and chemoattractant transcriptional programs, and remodeling of endothelial–myeloid ligand–receptor communication. We find that microglial reprogramming is accompanied by coordinated changes in chromatin accessibility and heightened activity of the AP-1 transcription factor complex. records.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Unveils Macrophage Involvement in Aortic Valve Stenosis Progression [spatial transcriptome]
records.summary: Introduction: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is an age-related progressive disease with increasing global prevalence. Although chronic inflammation is a key factor in its pathogenesis, the detailed immune cell profiles and their interactions with non-immune cells remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize the immune cell landscape in calcific AS at a single-cell level and evaluate the potential of anti-inflammatory therapy. Methods: Human aortic valve samples were obtained from four patients with non-calcified aortic regurgitation (AR) and 11 patients with AS undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. Single-cell 3’ gene expression sequencing (scRNA-seq (3’)) was performed on CD45+ immune cells, while single-cell RNA sequencing Flex (scRNA-seq (Flex)) and bulk RNA sequencing were conducted on unsorted cells. Additionally, an anti-TNFα antibody experiment was performed in a murine AS model induced by aortic valve wire injury. Results: In myeloid cells, LYVE1 resident macrophages were significantly decreased, whereas classical monocytes expressing pro-inflammatory genes and C1Q macrophages were increased in AS valves compared to AR valves. These macrophages exhibited strong interactions with valve interstitial cells, particularly with chondrogenic subtypes express
evidence: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Unveils Macrophage Involvement in Aortic Valve Stenosis Progression [spatial transcriptome].

Single-cell 3’ gene expression sequencing (scRNA-seq (3’)) was performed on CD45+ immune cells, while single-cell RNA sequencing Flex (scRNA-seq (Flex)) and bulk RNA sequencing were conducted on unsorted cells.

Conclusions: This study is the first to integrate scRNA-seq (3’) and scRNA-seq (Flex) analyses of human aortic valves, revealing single cell-level characteristics of immune cells and their interactions with non-immune cells in calcific AS.

records.title: Cellular and Molecular Changes Underpinning the Formation of Intimal Hyperplasia in a Model of Static Human Saphenous Vein Ex Vivo Culture
records.summary: Intimal hyperplasia (IH) significantly limits the long-term patency of saphenous vein grafts following bypass surgery, with no with no widely accepted human models that fully captures its complex pathogenesis. Although animal models, primarily murine systems, have provided mechanistic insights into IH, limitations persist in translating these findings to human pathophysiology. Human saphenous vein segments obtained from patients who underwent lower limb bypass surgery were cultured ex vivo for 7 days under static conditions. Bulk RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics (GeoMx) were employed to characterize the localized transcriptional alterations. Cultured vein segments developed characteristic features of IH, including marked endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC) apoptosis and proliferation, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and neointima formation. Spatial transcriptomics revealed localized VSMC dedifferentiation and activation of inflammatory, oxidative stress, and ECM remodelling pathways. We further observed upregulation of osteogenic markers Sox9 and RunX2, and RunX2 inhibition limited IH.

records.title: Vascular smooth muscle cell abundance is a hallmark of Castleman Disease
records.summary: Castleman Disease (CD) is a poorly understood inflammatory disorder characterized by enlarged lymph nodes with distinctive histologic features. Its opaque pathophysiology delays diagnoses and limits treatments, leading to additional morbidity and mortality. Since lymph nodes are the key lesional tissue for the disease, we sought to better understand the molecular and cellular underpinnings of CD lymph nodes using single cell and spatial transcriptomics. We found pronounced alterations in cell composition and dysregulation of distinct molecular pathways in non-hematopoietic stromal cells in lymph nodes from the unicentric form of CD. In contrast, hematopoietic cells in CD lymph nodes showed only few compositional or expression changes when compared to enlarged lymph nodes with non-specific inflammation. The elevated abundance of vascular smooth muscle cells, a subset of lymph node stromal cells, in unicentric CD lymph nodes and broadly increased stromal cell activity signified CD lymph nodes. In particular, immunohistochemical staining for the vascular smooth muscle cell marker CD146 (Melanoma Cell Adhesion Molecule, MCAM) served as reliable discriminator of unicentric CD lymph nodes from related lymphadenopathies. evidence: Since lymph nodes are the key lesional tissue for the disease, we sought to better understand the molecular and cellular underpinnings of CD lymph nodes using single cell and spatial transcriptomics.
In sum, single cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses of CD lymph nodes facilitate the identification of CD-specific molecular and cellular features to guide diagnosis and patient stratification.

records.title: Shared molecular regulation of quiescence in neural and glioma stem cells reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities
records.summary: Quiescent glioma cells evade chemoradiation and drive glioblastoma recurrence by reactivating to repopulate the tumour, but are hard to study due to their rarity and difficulty maintaining quiescence in vitro. We hypothesised that quiescence programs conserved between neural stem cells and glioma cells could be exploited to lock glioma cells in quiescence and prevent reactivation. Using single-cell RNA-sequencing and patient-derived glioma stem cell lines, we found that although glioma cells resist entering deep quiescence, they share conserved activation trajectories with neural stem cells. Because this conservation lets a tractable neural progenitor line act as a surrogate for rare quiescent glioma cells, we queried LINCS L1000 signatures across more than 3,000 compounds and validated the top classes (mTOR, ATPase and histone lysine methyltransferase inhibitors) as quiescence promoters in glioma stem cell lines. By establishing conserved activation programs and enabling cross-cell-type screening, our work provides a strategy for driving therapy-resistant glioma cells into quiescence.
evidence: Using single-cell RNA-sequencing and patient-derived glioma stem cell lines, we found that although glioma cells resist entering deep quiescence, they share conserved activation trajectories with neural stem cells.

records.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Immune Cell Profiles in Lower Extremity Artery Disease Plaques
records.summary: Backgrounds Lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) is a common manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis and is frequently associated with coronary and cerebrovascular disease. Although lipid-lowering therapy and risk factor control are essential, residual inflammatory risk remains a key determinant of adverse outcomes. Given the established link between inflammation and immune cells, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to characterize immune cell populations in lower extremity arterial plaques from patients with LEAD, comparing advanced chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions with relatively early non-CTO lesions. Results Single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45⁺ immune cells from five CTO and five non-CTO lower extremity artery plaques identified seven major clusters, predominantly T cells and myeloid cells. KLRD1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells tended to be more abundant in CTO lesions (p = 0.072). Re-clustering of CD4⁺ T cells identified five subsets, including FOXP3⁺ regulatory, cytotoxic, naïve, and central memory T cells, without statistically significant differences between CTO and non-CTO lesions. records.title: IL-31 Blockade Elevates TARC by Lifting LAMP3+ CD1c+ Mature Dendritic Cells from CGRP-CALCRL Neuroimmune Suppression in Atopic Dermatitis [human]
records.summary: Background: Nemolizumab reduces pruritus and skin lesions in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD), yet some patients develop cutaneous adverse events (CAEs) with increased serum thymus and activation regulated chemokine (TARC); mechanisms are unclear. Objective: Define systemic changes and the mechanism underlying TARC elevation after IL 31 receptor A (IL 31RA) blockade. Methods: Serum proteomics (Olink), MC903 models ± anti IL 31RA, skin single cell RNA seq of AD skin with in situ validation, functional assays using human dendritic cells (DCs), and human dorsal root ganglion analyses with ligand–receptor inference were integrated. Results: In patients with CAEs, TARC levels increased and correlated with type 2 markers. In mice, IL 31 RA blockade increased serum and dermal TARC without broad transcriptomic shifts. A Ccl17 T2A GFP reporter localized TARC to dermal DCs, enriched in type 2 conventional dendritic cell (cDC2). In patients, CCL17 localized to LAMP3⁺ CD1c⁺ mature DCs in situ. Analyses supported calcitonin gene–related peptide (CGRP) signaling via the calcitonin receptor-like (CALCRL) signaling from IL31-RA/oncostatin M receptor (OSMR) positive nociceptors to mature DCs; CGRP reduced DC maturation and TARC in vitro. Conclusion: Findings support an IL 31–dependent CGRP–CA

records.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Decodes Cell-Specific Non-Coding Landscapes in Human Cardiogenesis and Congenital Heart Disease
records.summary: Contemporary single-cell epigenomic studies have identified important unresolved questions regarding chromatin dynamics in cardiac development. Leveraging our SpliCoTECH platform - an innovative single-cell multi-omics approach combining transcriptomic and chromatin binding profiling - we defined six chromatin states per metacell and mapped 610 high-scoring ncDNVs to specific chromatin contexts during hESC-CM differentiation. Here, through SpliCoTECH-RNA profiling, we further characterized functional ncDNV in understudied repressive chromatin domains, revealing its roles in modulating gene expression and lineage commitment. These findings uncover a sophisticated interplay between chromatin architecture and transcriptional regulation during cardiogenesis.

records.title: 14 primary formalin fixated paraffin embedded (FFPE) PDAC tissue slices from 14 patients without pretreatment were analyzed using spatial transcriptomics
records.summary: spatial transcriptomics by high-throughput sequencing Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound molecular heterogeneity and poor prognosis, necessitating novel tailored therapies. The basal and classical molecular subtypes of PDAC - driven by glycolysis versus lipid metabolism - have distinct prognostic implications. Spatial transcriptomics using FFPE tissue from 14 primary PDAC tumors was performed to spatially map PDAC molecular subtype heterogeneity. Our analysis resolved cancer cell signatures, deconvoluted intra-tumoral heterogeneity, and delineated a classical-to-basal trajectory.

records.title: ERK1/2 Inhibition Overcomes Resistance to Venetoclax in AML by Inhibiting Drp1-Dependent Mitochondrial Fission and Destabilizing Mcl-1 [scRNA-Seq 2]
records.summary: ERK1/2-mediated phosphorylation of Drp1 drives mitochondrial fission, stemness, and therapy resistance in RAS-driven solid tumors; however, its role in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains unclear. We identified ERK1/2-mediated Drp1 phosphorylation as a mechanism of resistance to venetoclax in AML. ERK1/2 inhibition using Compound 27 (ERKi), an analog of the clinical ERK1/2 inhibitor ASTX029, reduced mitochondrial fission, induced ROS accumulation, mitochondrial depolarization, and apoptosis in venetoclax-resistant AML cells. ERKi sensitized resistant AML cells to venetoclax and depleted leukemia progenitor cells in primary AML samples. Conversely, overexpression of Drp1-phosphomimetic restored mitochondrial fission and reversed apoptosis induced by venetoclax alone and in combination with ERKi. In post-venetoclax/decitabine relapsed human AML PDX model, co-treatment with venetoclax and ASTX029 improved survival and reduced leukemia burden accompanied by decreased pDrp1-Ser616, Mcl-1, and pMcl-1-Thr163 expression in bone marrow-derived human leukemic cells. In conclusion, inhibiting the ERK1/2-Drp1 axis overcomes resistance to venetoclax in AML.
evidence: ERK1/2 Inhibition Overcomes Resistance to Venetoclax in AML by Inhibiting Drp1-Dependent Mitochondrial Fission and Destabilizing Mcl-1 [scRNA-Seq 2].

records.title: A multimodal precision oncology platform integrating genomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional drug screening expands therapeutic options in pediatric brain tumors
records.summary: Precision oncology for pediatric brain tumors relies on clinically validated, targetable genomic alterations, which are often sparse, yield few matched therapies, and do not guide chemotherapy selection. We developed a tiered framework in which deep whole-genome sequencing and single-cell RNA sequencing extend targeted-therapy selection, whereas ex vivo functional drug screening supports selection of both targeted therapies and chemotherapies. We applied it to 17 children with CNS tumors. The approach expanded recommendations beyond genomics: functional screening provided every patient with at least one high-confidence targeted-therapy or chemotherapy nomination, while single-cell RNA sequencing identified an average of 37 druggable gene targets per patient, producing a fourfold increase in high-confidence targeted-therapy recommendations. In an exploratory analysis, functional classifications were directionally consistent with outcomes in 8 of 10 evaluable cases, although combination treatments and radiation precluded causal attribution. Single-cell profiling also identified subclone-specific vulnerabilities, supporting prospective evaluation of the platform’s feasibility and predictive utility.

records.title: Sex Steroid Hormone Signaling Tunes Metabolic and Neuronal Programs in Human Cortical Development
records.summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) exhibits a profound male biased sex ratio. While numerous genes have been implicated in ASD, the functional basis of this sex difference is unclear. One enticing hypothesis is genome-wide transcriptional regulation through estrogens and androgens. While hormone-mediated transcription is well-studied in reproductive tissues, its role in cortical development is poorly defined. Thus, we profiled androgen (AR) and estrogen (ESR1/ESR2) receptor expression in primary human cortex and developmental stage-matched organoid models by single-cell RNA-seq. AR was primarily expressed in radial glia and intermediate progenitors while ESR1/ESR2 was more broadly distributed across multiple cell types of the developing cortex, although with the highest expression in radial glia. To study their genetic effects, we exposed iNeurons and cortical organoids to physiological levels of dihydro-testosterone (DHT) and estradiol (E2). DHT consistently up-regulated oxidative metabolism programs enriched in progenitor cells and down-regulated neuronal maturation pathways, while E2 exhibited a much more attenuated effect. records.summary: Intestinal homeostasis crucially depends on functional epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. Perturbations therein can drive fibrosis, a severe but common complication of advanced inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). records.title: Lung neuroendocrine cancer induces immunosuppressive macrophages via serotonin to drive resistance to the T cell engager tarlatamab [Xenium]
records.summary: Tarlatamab, a DLL3/CD3-directed T-cell engager (TCE), provides clinical efficacy against small cell lung cancers (SCLCs), although its efficacy remains limited, indicating the importance of clarifying the resistance mechanism(s). Here, we show that serotonin (5-HT) produced by DLL3high neuroendocrine cancers (NECs) induces immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), resulting in impaired CD8+ T-cell function and TCE resistance. Using patient cohorts with SCLC and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC), we found that DLL3high SCLCs induced immunosuppressive TAMs in the tumor microenvironment and became resistant to tarlatamab. DLL3high NECs increased 5-HT production via TPH1 upregulation. NEC-derived 5-HT augmented the immunosuppressive activity of 5-HT receptor 7 (HTR7)-expressing TAMs. Genetic ablation of HTR7 in TAMs or TPH1 in NECs restored CD8+ T-cell function and improved the efficacy of TCEs and PD-1 blockade. We propose that the NEC-derived 5-HT–HTR7 axis drives immunosuppressive TAM activation and TCE resistance, making it a key target to increase TCE efficacy.
evidence: Lung neuroendocrine cancer induces immunosuppressive macrophages via serotonin to drive resistance to the T cell engager tarlatamab [Xenium].

records.title: Landscape of the Tumor Microenvironment and Cellular Mechanisms in Pancreatic Cancer During Cachexia Progression
records.summary: Cancer progression is associated with dynamic crosstalk between malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the spatiotemporal mechanisms of the TME during cachexia progression remain poorly understood. Therefore, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk transcriptomic analyses to reveal the molecular trajectories across the non-cachexia (non-CAC), pre-cachexia (Pre-CAC), and cachexia (CAC) stages. We identified a progressively expanding SEMA4A+ tumor subcluster with pro-inflammatory properties that directly induces muscle atrophy via SEMA4A, whose expression gradually increases during cachexia progression in PC patients. Importantly, SEMA4A+ tumor cells reprogram TME through polarizing macrophages towards an AQP9+ phenotype. In turn, these AQP9+ macrophages drive cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) into LOXL2+ CAFs. LOXL2+ CAFs subsequently facilitate FOSL1 and SEMA4A expression in tumor cells, establishing a self-reinforcing signaling circuit that promote PC cachexia. This cascade culminates in the formation of a triadic niche that drives cachexia progression in PC.
evidence: Therefore, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk transcriptomic analyses to reveal the molecular trajectories across the non-cachexia (non-CAC), pre-cachexia (Pre-CAC), and cachexia (CAC) stages.

records.title: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of human cortical brain organoids profiles transcriptional responses to amyloid-beta fibrils and their modulation by the J8 single-domain antibody in an Alzheimer's disease model
records.summary: We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to investigate transcriptional changes in human cortical brain organoids modeling Alzheimer's disease. Organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were exposed to amyloid-beta fibrils to induce disease-relevant pathology, with or without co-treatment with the J8 single-domain antibody. Three experimental conditions were analyzed: untreated control, amyloid-beta fibril-treated (Fibrils), and fibril plus J8-treated (FibJ8). This dataset provides a cell-type-resolved view of responses to amyloid-beta pathology and examines the potential modulatory effects of J8 co-treatment.

records.title: An integrated breast cancer transcriptomic atlas defines clinical subtypes and informs cellular origin
records.summary: Efforts to analyze breast cancer transcriptomes at scale have been limited by cross-study technical variability. To address this, we adapted single cell RNA sequencing analytical strategies to harmonize 7,612 bulk breast cancer transcriptomes from 22 datasets, generating a high resolution atlas that resolves both known and previously unrecognized malignant transcriptional states. This framework identified existing intrinsic subtypes, microenvironmental programs, and newly identified stem like, basal-luminal progenitor (BLP), mucinous, and neuroendocrine differentiated (NED) subtypes, each displaying distinct clinical behaviors. The NED subtype exhibited luminal features, neuroendocrine marker expression, and associated with chemo-endocrine therapy poor prognosis. The HER2E-kinase inhibitor sensitive (HER2EKIS) subtype identified patients who achieved high pCR rate from HER2-targeted kinase inhibitors. Transcriptomic positioning of BLP tumors suggests a bipotent or myoepithelial progenitor association, limited responsiveness to chemotherapy, and potential benefit to VEGF and receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors. This atlas refines breast cancer subtype classification and provides a framework for guiding therapy and understanding tumor origins.
evidence: To address this, we adapted single cell RNA sequencing analytical strategies to harmonize 7,612 bulk breast cancer transcriptomes from 22 datasets, generating a high resolution atlas that resolves both known and previously unrecognized malignant transcriptional states.

records.title: Tumor-intrinsic and extrinsic immune mechanisms define resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic melanoma [tcr]
records.summary: The interplay between variable genomic, transcriptional, and microenvironmental features driving resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains poorly understood. Here, we performed multi-omic profiling (single-nucleus RNA, T cell receptor, and whole-genome sequencing) of 42 sequential biopsies from 34 patients with metastatic melanoma. Using a Bayesian integrative model, we identify recurring features of ICB-sensitive and resistant clones, and uncouple gene dosage effects from transcriptional output, thereby defining genetic and non-genetic basis for plasticity. Joint characterization of tumor-immune microenvironment uncovered evolution of malignant and immune cells with ICB treatment, capturing clinically relevant shifts in T cell states and macrophage polarization. Co-evolving crosstalk among malignant and immune compartments defined clone‑specific immune‑evasion circuits, including erosion of the CD58-CD2 axis. This study provides a unified framework for disentangling complex intra- and inter-cellular genotype-phenotype interactions, and shows that evolving immune dysfunction ensues upon prolonged exposure to ICB, thus informing clinical practice in melanoma and beyond.
evidence: Here, we performed multi-omic profiling (single-nucleus RNA, T cell receptor, and whole-genome sequencing) of 42 sequential biopsies from 34 patients with metastatic melanoma.

records.title: Inhibition of a corrupted embryonic developmental regulator reverses colon cancer to a normal-like state [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: Transforming the malignant characteristics of cancer cells instead of killing them is one potential strategy to overcome limitations associated with cancer therapies intended to induce cancer cell apoptosis. A systems approach could identify mechanisms to drive the reversion of cancer cells into normal-like cells. Here, we identify the transition state between normal and cancer cells in colon and show that knockdown of TATA-box-binding-protein-associated Factor 10 (TAF10) can rewire the gene regulatory network, resulting in reversion of colon cancer cells into normal-like cells. Intriguingly, TAF10 is essential in embryonic development and should be inactivated after development, but is instead hijacked during colon cancer tumorigenesis and remains as a potential reversion switch of the underlying complex molecular network.

records.title: Colorectal cancer heterogeneity co-evolves with tumor architecture to determine disease outcome [scRNA-seq]

records.title: Functional Merlin Depletion Defines a TEAD1-Dependent Tumor Cell State that Promotes Schwannoma Progression: Xenium spatial transcriptomics
records.summary: Biallelic loss of the tumor suppressor NF2/merlin drives vestibular schwannomas (VS). Intratumoral heterogeneity has been observed in VS at the transcriptional, protein expression, and cellular proliferative potential levels, highlighting the need to elucidate the mechanisms underlying heterogeneity in tumor Schwann cell merlin inactivation and therapeutic resistance. Using integrated single-cell multi-omic profiling across NF2-related (VSnf2) and sporadic (VSspo) schwannomas, we identified functional merlin depletion as a continuous, spatially organized, plastic tumor Schwann cell state, rather than a binary genetic event. A transcriptomic merlin depletion score (MDS) captured this gradient, and merlin-depleted tumor Schwann cells were identified as a potential source of proliferative, angiogenic, and macrophage-recruiting signals. Lineage trajectory and multi-omic regulatory modeling identified the transcription factor TEAD1 as a potential regulator of MDS states and signaling pathways underlying tumor progression. records.title: A single cell and spatial atlas of preinvasive breast cancer
records.summary: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. This Series only contains the Xenium samples, for the Visium samples see GSE348919.

records.title: Spatial Transcriptomics to Investigate the Impact of HIV/ART on DLBCL Tumorigenesis and Tumor Microenvironment
records.summary: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and tumor heterogeneity shape prognosis and therapeutic response in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), but HIV-associated DLBCL remains poorly understood. We performed spatial transcriptomics on pre-treatment DLBCL biopsies to characterize the TIME and tumor-intrinsic features across a spectrum of HIV-associated immune dysregulation. Our analysis revealed distinct immune architectures shaped by HIV status and antiretroviral therapy (ART) exposure, with implications for immunotherapeutic strategies in a population historically excluded from such trials.

records.title: Identification and Characterization of Adrenergic and Mesenchymal Cancer Cell States in Neuroblastoma Using Spatial-Omics [RNA-Seq]
records.summary: Neuroblastoma is a pediatric cancer arising from the developing sympathoadrenal lineage and cell lines derived from neuroblastoma patients have features of either adrenergic neurons (ADRN) or mesenchymal cells (MES). However, identification of MES neuroblastoma cells in patient tumors has been challenging and controversial. This may be due to inter- or intra-patient tumor heterogeneity or discrepancies between the established neuroblastoma cell lines and patient tumors. To characterize the intra- and inter-patient cellular heterogeneity, we analyzed 54 neuroblastoma tumors, spanning a broad range of clinical, genetic, and histologic features. We combined single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq (sc/scRNA-seq), bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial proteomics. We discovered that the tumor cells are in distinct cellular neighborhoods from the non-malignant immune and stromal cells, but we could not identify MES neuroblastoma cells using the established gene expression signatures developed from cell lines. However, using ADRN/MES gene expression signatures developed from early passage orthotopic patient-derived xenografts, we were able to identify MES neuroblastoma tumor cells. records.title: Exploratory Single-nucleus Multiomics of Myeloid Cell States Associated with Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Human Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
records.summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a complex tumor microenvironment that may be altered by neoadjuvant chemotherapy. As part of an exploratory multi-omics study focused on lipid-associated macrophages (LAMs), we performed 10x Genomics Visium CytAssist spatial transcriptomic profiling of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded PDAC tumor specimens. This dataset includes spatial transcriptomic profiles from one chemotherapy-treated PDAC tumor and one untreated PDAC tumor specimen. The spatial transcriptomics analysis was designed to evaluate the spatial distribution and expression of LAM-associated gene programs within PDAC tissue sections. Spatial gene expression libraries were generated using the 10x Genomics Visium FFPE workflow and sequenced on an Illumina platform. Data were processed using Space Ranger, followed by downstream analysis to identify macrophage-predominant regions and examine the expression of LAM-associated genes, including APOE, PPARG, GPNMB, and GLUL. This dataset provides a spatial transcriptomic resource to examine LAM-like macrophage gene expression patterns in PDAC and to generate hypotheses about chemotherapy-associated changes in LAM-related programs within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment.

records.overall_design: PDAC tumor specimens, which include a chemotherapy responder PDAC sample and an untreated PDAC sample, were fixed and embedded in paraffin blocks and stored at −80 °C until sectioning. Blocks were equilibrated to the cryostat chamber (−20 °C). Tissue was sectioned at 10 µm and mounted onto positively charged glass slides compatible with the 10x Genomics Visium CytAssist workflow. For the FFPE samples, 4 x 10-μm FFPE sections were collected for RNA extraction by RNeasy FFPE Kit (Qiagen, 73504). DV200 of the yielded RNA was evaluated using Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit. Samples with DV200>30% were selected for sectioning, deparaffinization, and H&E staining on the Visium Spatial Slide with 6.5 x 6.5 mm capture area. Probe hybridization, probe ligation, probe release & extension, and library construction were conducted following the Visium Spatial Gene Expression Reagent Kit for FFPE User Guide (10x Genomics, CG000407 Rev A). To capture the area of interest, the samples were selected for Visium CytAssist, which facilitates the transfer of transcriptomic probes from standard glass slides to Visium slides, enabling whole-transcriptomic spatial profiling. Briefly, the slides were stained by H&E and imaged at ×20 magnification. Using the Visium CytAssist instrument and disposable fiducial frame, stained sections on standard glass were aligned and transferred onto the capture area of a Visium Gene Expression slide according to our WVU Flow Cytometry & Single Cell Core Facility’s SOP adapted directly from the 10x Genomics manual (CG000495, RevB). Representative regions with at least 2 nerves within a 6.5x6.5 mm area were selected by an appropriate configuration that allows the tissue slide gasket to encompass the region of interest. Then the coverslips were removed, and the slides were destained by 0.1N HCl and decrosslinked by Diluted Decrosslinking Buffer at 95°C for 1 h (10x Genomics, CG000658, RevA). Probe hybridization and probe ligation were processed according to the user guide (10x Genomics, CG000495, RevB). Then the hybridized probes were released and transferred to a Visium CytAssist Spatial Gene Expression Slide. After transfer, probes were extended, eluted, and pre-amplified. Then, the Sample Index PCR was applied to construct the cDNA library. The libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 2000 sequencer at the Marshall University Genomics Core Facility.

records.title: Complex Human Hair Bearing Skin Organoids Reveal Cell-Type Specific Susceptibility and Innate Immune Responses to Herpes Simplex Virus 1
records.summary: Epithelial surfaces are the initial site of Herpes Simplex Virus 1 (HSV-1) infection. To reflect the complexity of human skin, we used complex human hair bearing skin organoids as a new model system for HSV-1 infection. Using microscopy and spatial transcriptomics with single cell resolution, we characterize the progression of infection through the tissue as well as host cell responses.

records.summary: Endometrial dysfunction in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) significantly contributes to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including recurrent implantation failure and high miscarriage rates. However, the specific roles of individual cell types in this dysfunction, particularly in non-obese and obese PCOS patients, remain unclear. records.title: Single-cell analysis reveals epithelial alarmin-associated immune architecture in pediatric refractory and rhinovirus-positive asthma
records.summary: Background: Asthma in children is increasingly recognized as biologically distinct from adult disease, yet the cellular organization underlying refractory asthma and virus-associated exacerbation remains poorly defined. In particular, how chronic airway remodeling and acute viral responses are integrated within the pediatric airway microenvironment is not well understood. Methods:Children with asthma were classified into refractory asthma (defined according to Global Initiative for Asthma criteria) and rhinovirus-positive asthma (defined by qPCR-confirmed rhinovirus infection). Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples from children with refractory asthma (n = 5), rhinovirus-positive asthma (n = 4) and healthy controls (n = 6) were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing, followed by integrative bioinformatic analysis and cross-age comparison with adult asthma datasets. Controls were obtained from individuals undergoing bronchoscopy for non-inflammatory indications and lacked a history of atopy or airway inflammatory disease. records.title: Meniscus-On-a-Chip model to delineate multi-tissue crosstalk
records.summary: Meniscus has been largely ignored for the emerging research interest of multi-tissue crosstalk in knee joints. This study discovers the novel roles of three-way crosstalk between meniscus, synovial membrane, and fat in regulation of meniscus injury, degeneration, and healing. A novel meniscus-on-a-chip (MoC) model is developed, equipped with bioprinted synovial membrane, engineered fat tissue, and meniscus explant healing model, treated with bioactive glue and synovial mesenchymal stem cells (syMSCs). Our MoC integrated with meniscus-specific bioreactor enables a comprehensive investigation into the combinational effects of inflammation and physiological/pathological loading on meniscus healing and degeneration. The MoC successfully not only replicates meniscus healing induced by bioactive glue but also the OA initiation and progression from meniscus injury. Comprehensive scRNA-seq with CellChat analysis discovers how communications between adipocytes, macrophages, fibrochondrocytes, and syMSCs regulate the fate of meniscus injury in response to exogenous stimulations. records.summary: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), or myositis, are a group of systemic autoimmune diseases leading to proximal muscle weakness. Myocarditis is estimated to affect up to 50% of IIM patients and is a major cause of adverse outcomes in these patients. Yet, we know very little about the underlying immunologic processes that are driving myocarditis in the context of IIM. records.title: Targeting glucocorticoid-induced CD20 activation in preclinical models of B-ALL
records.summary: Pediatric B‑cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B‑ALL) is effectively controlled with contemporary multi-agent chemotherapy, resulting to 5‑year survival rates above 90%. However, relapse occurs in 15-20% of patients due to minimal residual disease (MRD), characterized by the presence of persisting and resistant leukemic cells, and associated with a poor clinical outcome. Despite its prognostic relevance, the molecular features driving MRD are poorly characterized. In this study, we developed patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models from matched diagnosis and relapse B‑ALL samples combined to chemotherapy to mimic MRD in vivo. Drug-tolerant leukemic cells were profiled using single-cell RNA sequencing and we identified a transcriptionally distinct MRD-like population enriched for cell-quiescence, inflammatory stress, and B‑cell receptor pathway signatures. records.title: NKX2.2 regulates endocrine commitment via metabolic regulation of NEUROG3 progenitors [scRNA-seq]
records.summary: In mice and humans, the four major populations of adult pancreatic islet cells are derived from a common Neurogenin3 (NEUROG3)-expressing endocrine progenitor population. NKX2.2 is also expressed in the developing human pancreas and individuals carrying homozygous null mutations in NKX2.2 present with neonatal diabetes and have undetectable serum levels of insulin at birth, suggesting a conserved developmental function. records.title: Liver Disease Reveals KIF12 as a Critical Regulator of Organelle Localization
records.summary: Kinesin family member 12 (KIF12) has been implicated in liver disease requiring transplantation in pediatric patients. Single cell RNA-sequencing shows KIF12 expression selectively in biliary cells in healthy human liver. Here, we generated a human KIF12-disease model by introducing a homozygous KIF12 p.Arg219* mutation in induced pluripotent stem cells. These cells were differentiated into 2D cholangiocyte-like cells (iCCs) and 3D biliary organoids. Pioneering single-molecule fluorescence microscopy in live iCCs, we observed wild-type KIF12 co-localizing with microtubules, consistent with prediction of being a microtubule associated motor protein. KIF12 deficiency causes perinuclear clustering of mitochondria and lysosomes, along with aberrant cilia localization. These defects were rescued by viral delivery of wild-type KIF12. Collectively, these findings uncovered a mechanistic link between KIF12 dysfunction, mitochondria, lysosomes, and cilia mispositioning, and biliary pathology. Our study expands the knowledge of kinesins beyond neuronal function and provides a foundation for development of targeted genetic therapies for kinesinopathies.
evidence: Single cell RNA-sequencing shows KIF12 expression selectively in biliary cells in healthy human liver.

records.title: Single-cell RNA-seq profiling of ARID1A-loss-associated transcriptional heterogeneity and clonal diversification in pancreatic cancer cells
records.summary: This Series contains additional single-cell RNA-seq datasets associated with a study of how loss of epigenetic regulators, particularly ARID1A, reshapes transcriptional heterogeneity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells. The shPseuMO-Tag system couples genetic perturbation with clonal lineage tracing. The datasets include an initial epigenetic-modifier screen, an ARID1A knockdown time course, a large-scale pooled five-shRNA experiment, acute SMARCA4 degradation, independent experiments in multiple PDAC cell lines, and matched pre-injection and lung-colonization samples. In the independent multi-cell-line experiment, BxPC3, HPAC, SW1990, and SUIT-2 were profiled using independently derived clones, whereas HPAFII was analyzed as a pooled population because stable single-cell-derived HPAFII clones could not be established.

records.title: Fibroblast–myeloid stromal crosstalk is associated with clinicopathological diversity and clinical outcome in intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms of the pancreas
records.summary: We sequenced four single-nucleus RNA (snRNA) libraries from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissued of pancreatic intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) with distinct histological grades and subtypes. The snRNA sequencing revealed that fibroblasts were the main source of cell–cell communication, whereas myeloid and mast cells were the main receivers. Therefore, we subclassified fibroblasts into inflammatory (iCAF), myofibroblast (myCAF), and reticular-like (rCAF) subpopulations, and myeloid cells into monocytes, neutrophils, macrophages, and dendritic subpopulations. Additional analyses revealed that iCAF and rCAF mainly communicated with SPP1^High macrophages and neutrophils via inflammatory pathways. Conversely, myCAF mainly communicated with monocytes and mast cells via ECM-associated pathways.

records.title: A Scalable Human Brain Cell Atlas Dissects the Microglial Immune Codes and Cognitive Resilience
records.summary: The biological basis of resilience to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains unclear, hindering the development of effective interventions for brain health. Here, we present the largest human brain single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas to date (~14 million nuclei across 31 brain regions from 2,239 deeply phenotyped postmortem samples, including cognitively normal (CN), AD (clinico-pathologically confirmed), cognitively resilient (CR), and primary age-related tauopathy (PART)), using a scalable generative artificial intelligence framework. This resource identifies >50 neuronal and glial cell types and reveals a linkage of mitochondrial bioenergetics in somatostatin (SST) neurons to cognitive resilience in the presence of amyloid-beta and tau pathology, which we validated immunohistochemically. We also identified that the microglia-associated genes PLCG2 and GPNMB were associated with AD progression in an age-independent manner. Genes encoding interferon signaling pathways (e.g., IFIT3 and IFI44) were identified as female-specific markers in disease-associated microglia. We also identified glutamate signaling-mediated immune-neuron crosstalks associated with AD etiologies, which was experimentally validated by transcriptomic signatures in patient iPSC-derived microglia. records.title: A bispecific CD3×CD19 antibody for systemic lupus erythematosus: a phase 1 trial
records.summary: Deep CD19-directed B cell depletion has induced prolonged, drug-free remission in refractory autoimmune disease through elimination of pathogenic B cell populations and reset of downstream inflammatory networks. CD19 CAR T cell therapy—which has shown remarkable promise in early-phase studies—requires lymphodepleting chemotherapy, autologous cell manufacturing, and specialized infrastructure, limiting its reach to a fraction of patients who might benefit. Bispecific T-cell engagers (TCEs) offer a potent, off-the-shelf approach to peripheral and tissue B cell depletion; however, controlled clinical evaluation in rheumatic disease remains limited. records.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analyses of severe Covid-19 lungs identifies disease-associated spatial niches
records.summary: Severe COVID-19 is characterized by marked heterogeneity in lung pathology, yet how spatially organized cellular interactions shape disease progression remains unclear. Here, we applied imaging-based single-cell spatial transcriptomics to post-mortem lung samples from severe COVID-19 patients and controls. We identified distinct cellular niches associated with specific histopathological states, including fibrotic and alveolar remodeling regions. Fibrotic niches were enriched in CHI3L1/MMP9hi macrophages spatially associated with COL1A1+ fibroblasts and predicted to drive pathogenic fibroblast reprogramming through Tgf-β and galectin-3 signaling. In contrast, alveolar niches contained SPP1hi macrophages exposed to epithelial-derived cues, including WNT ligands and GM-CSF, consistent with differentiation toward an alveolar macrophage-like state. These findings reveal that severe COVID-19 lungs are organized into discrete, macrophage-centered microenvironments that differentially regulate tissue remodeling, providing a spatial framework to understand divergent immunopathological trajectories.

Mechanistically, RNF43659mut-mediated PI3K/AKT activation induced HLA-E expression, suppressing NK cell function. Pharmacological or siRNA-mediated PI3K/AKT inhibition restored NK cell activity and enhanced tumor cell killing. records.title: A single chromosome 3p break initiates clear cell renal cell carcinoma evolution
records.summary: We used single-cell RNA sequencing (10x Genomics) coupled with CITE-seq cell hashing (HTO) to profile and compare the transcriptomes of renal proximal tubule epithelial cells (RPTECs) after different CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) perturbations. Cells were treated with a non-targeting control sgRNA (sgNTC), an sgRNA targeting chromosome 3p (sg3p), or an sgRNA targeting chromosome Yq (sgYq), and harvested at Day 5 and Day 10. Hashtag-labeled samples were pooled into three 10x Chip G lanes, and gene-expression and HTO libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus. Copy-number alterations were inferred (inferCNV) to identify cells with chromosome 3p loss, and differential gene expression was compared between 3p-loss and no-loss populations over time.

records.title: Autism-relevant oxysterol signaling regulates GABAergic neurogenesis and interneuron subtype specification
records.summary: Distorted GABAergic neurodevelopment is believed to underscore cortical network dysfunction that lies at the heart of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) such as autism and schizophrenia. GABAergic neuron diversity is sculptured by cortical environmental cues during protracted postmitotic differentiation. However, the mechanism by which NDD environments influence GABAergic neuronal development remains largely unknown. Oxysterols are oxidized metabolites of cholesterol that can interact with developmental signaling pathways. Using an iPSC model recapitulating human forebrain GABAergic neuron development and single-cell transcriptomic profiling, we show that 24S, 25-epoxysterol, an NDD-associated oxysterol highly enriched in the fetal brain, promotes neurogenesis and disturbs the composition of neuronal subtypes. Moreover, pharmacological and genetic interrogation identified the liver X receptor as a regulatory pathway mediating the action of 24S, 25-epoxysterol. These findings provide insights into the roles played by cholesterol metabolism in neuronal development and a potential mechanism by which dysregulated brain oxysterols contribute to the pathogenesis of NDD.

records.title: Single-cell transcriptional landscape of gastric submucosal tumors (GISTs and GLMs) reveals antagonistic fibroblast–macrophage niches
records.summary: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) represent the most common mesenchymal neoplasm of the digestive tract. While targeted therapy with imatinib is standard, acquired resistance remains a major clinical challenge driven by incompletely defined microenvironmental mechanisms. To characterize the cellular landscape and identify microenvironmental determinants of therapy response, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on five prospectively collected, treatment-naïve gastric submucosal tumors, including three gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and two gastric leiomyomas (GLMs) as benign mesenchymal controls. Tissues were processed using the Singleron GEXSCOPE platform. Analysis of this dataset revealed that five transcriptionally distinct GIST tumor-cell states with distinct functional programs. Among these states, the S100A6-associated state (C2_S100A6) and the IGF2-associated state (C4_IGF2) showed opposing associations with imatinib response and distinct relationships with TAM programs.This dataset provides a high-resolution transcriptomic atlas of GIST and GLM, highlighting immunometabolic signatures relevant for risk stratification and therapeutic strategy.

records.title: RNA-binding protein CIRBP mediates PKM2 intron retention to negatively regulate multiple myeloma progression and macrophage alternative activation
records.summary: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a systemic malignancy characterized by the induction of osteolytic lesions. Cold-inducible RNA binding protein (CIRBP) has garnered attention in cancer research due to its dual role as either an oncogene or a tumor suppressor. In this study, publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data, MM cell lines, and an in vivo xenograft model are utilized to assess the biological significance of CIRBP in MM. Analysis reveals frequent communication between MM cells and macrophages, alongside decreased CIRBP expression in patients. Functionally, CIRBP overexpression in MM cells inhibits short- and long-term viability, suppresses proliferation, and reduces tumor burden in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, co-culture experiments confirm that CIRBP-expressing MM cells suppress macrophage chemotaxis and macrophage alternative activation, while CIRBP knockdown has opposite effects. Mechanistically, CIRBP binds to intron1 of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) precursor messenger RNA (pre-mRNA), inhibiting its splicing and promoting its nonsense-mediated decay, ultimately leading to downregulation of PKM2. records.title: Malignant ascites is associated with PIGR+RORC+ dendritic cell subset
records.summary: Malignant ascites is caused by the peritoneal dissemination of cancer and associated with a poor prognosis. We sought to identify unique features of the ascites microenvironment and leveraged single-cell RNA sequencing in patients with ascites from gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. We identified a dendritic cell (DC) subset that expresses RORC and foundt that this subset exists in low abundance in human tissues but is enriched in malignant ascites from multiple tumor histologies. We isolated and characterized this cell subset as a DC, and the expression of genes that define this subset can be induced by ascites supernatant. This DC subset appears to be associated with the peritoneal spread of cancer across tumor types and may help to provide opportunities to understand therapeutic resistance in the peritoneal cavity.
